definition_en: a main division of a book, a distinct period in a history or life, or a local branch of an organization
core_image: 一本书被书签分开的一段
scene: 夜深了，书页翻到新的部分。She stopped reading at the third chapter.
sceneCN: 这里 chapter 指「章」（第 1 个义项：书中的主要分节）；句意是她在第三章停下阅读。

senses.title: A main division of a book
senses.definition: one of the main parts into which a book or long text is divided
senses.definitionCN: 书或长文被分成的主要部分之一
senses.example: The first chapter sets the scene.
senses.exampleCN: 第一章交代了背景。
senses.why: Latin capitulum meant a little head, the heading written at the start of each section.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 capitulum 意为小头，即写在每节开头的小标题。

senses.title: A period in a life or history
senses.definition: a distinct period in someone's life or in the history of something
senses.definitionCN: 某人一生或某事历史中界限分明的一段
senses.example: That chapter of her life is closed.
senses.exampleCN: 她人生的那一章已经翻过去了。
senses.why: A section of a story was borrowed for a stretch of time that reads like a story.
senses.whyCN: 故事的一节被借来形容一段读起来像故事的时间。

senses.title: A local branch of a society
senses.definition: a local branch of a club, society or religious body
senses.definitionCN: 俱乐部、协会或宗教团体的地方分支
senses.example: The local chapter meets on Fridays.
senses.exampleCN: 地方分会每周五聚会。
senses.why: Members gathered under one heading formed a chapter, and the word passed to the group itself.
senses.whyCN: 在同一标题下聚集的成员构成一个 chapter，这个词又转指这群人本身。

intro.en: Chapter descends from Latin caput, a head, through the little heading written at the start of a section.
intro.cn: chapter 源自拉丁语 caput（头），经由写在一节开头的小标题而来。

items.en: Caput meant the head.
items.cn: 拉丁语 caput 意为头。

items.en: Capitulum was a little head, used for a heading.
items.cn: capitulum 意为小头，用来指标题。

items.en: Chapitre named a division of a book and a body of clergy.
items.cn: chapitre 指书中的分节，也指一群教士。

items.en: English chapter named both a book section and a cathedral body.
items.cn: 英语 chapter 同时指书中分节与主教座堂的教士团。

items.en: The word now also means a period of time and a local branch.
items.cn: 如今该词还指一段时期与地方分会。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the cap- head root, while the meaning group lists parts and phases.
note.cn: 形近组共享 cap-「头」词根，近义组列出部分与阶段。

entries.definition: the chief city or money for investment
the leader of a team or ship
more than one chapter
one part of a whole text
one event in a longer series
entries.definitionCN: 较长系列中的一个事件

entries.definition: a local office of an organization

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the head root, the phrase a new chapter and the local branch sense.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子利用「头」词根、短语 a new chapter 以及地方分会义。

normal.en: Chapter and capital share caput, the Latin head, because a chapter begins with a heading.
normal.cn: chapter 与 capital 共享拉丁语 caput（头），因为一章从一个标题开始。

normal.en: A new chapter is a fresh period, not a new book.
normal.cn: a new chapter 指新的阶段，而不是一本新书。

normal.en: Chapter and verse means you can cite the exact place.
normal.cn: chapter and verse 意为能引出确切出处。

normal.en: A local chapter is a branch that meets under one name.
normal.cn: local chapter 是在同一名下聚会的地方分支。

normal.en: The plural chapters adds an s and appears in chapter titles.
normal.cn: 复数 chapters 加 s，常出现在章节标题里。

abstract.en: Picture a bookmark closing one part of a story.
abstract.cn: 想象一枚书签合上故事的一段。

abstract.en: Picture a turned page with a large number at the top.
abstract.cn: 想象翻过的一页，顶端印着大大的数字。

abstract.en: Picture a small group of members raising hands in a side room.
abstract.cn: 想象一小群成员在小房间里举手。

examples.en: The book has twelve chapters.
examples.cn: 这本书有十二章。

examples.en: Moving abroad opened a new chapter in his life.
examples.cn: 移居国外为他的人生打开了新篇章。

examples.en: The student chapter organized a charity run.
examples.cn: 学生分会组织了一场慈善长跑。

dict_mnemonic.text: chapter 与 capital 同源，都来自「头」（caput）：一章就是一段文字的「头」。

root: 源自拉丁语 caput（头）的指小形式 capitulum（小头、标题），经古法语 chapitre 进入英语；与 capital、captain 同根。

sensesIntro.en: A heading marks off a book section, and that section became a period of time and a branch of members.
sensesIntro.cn: 标题划出书中的一节，这一节又变成一段时期与一群成员的分支。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a heading that opens a new section.
core.cn: 核心意象：开启新一节的那个标题。

branches.en: A chapter heading divides a long text.
branches.cn: 章节标题把长文分开。

branches.en: A closed chapter marks the end of a period.
branches.cn: 翻过去的一章标志一段时期的结束。

branches.en: A local chapter gathers members under one heading.
branches.cn: 地方分会在同一标题下聚集成员。

branches.en: Both senses borrow the shape of a story.
branches.cn: 两个义项都借用了故事的形态。

branches.en: Text divisions and member groups share the heading.
branches.cn: 文本分节与成员团体共享「标题」。

intro.en: Chapter keeps the cap- head root found in capital and captain.
intro.cn: chapter 保留在 capital 与 captain 中可见的 cap-「头」词根。

latinIntro.en: Latin caput and its diminutive capitulum are the head and the heading behind the word.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 caput 及其指小形式 capitulum 是这个词背后的「头」与「标题」。

items.meaning: a meeting house of a branch

items.example: The capital lies to the north.

latinEntries.exampleCN: caput 给出英语 capital。
capitulum 演变为 chapitre。

definition_en: the qualities that make a person or place distinct, a person in a story, or a letter or symbol used in writing
core_image: 刻在金属上的一枚印记，显示物件的本色
scene: 小说里的老人沉默而固执。The old man in the novel is a memorable character.
sceneCN: 这里 character 指「人物」（第 2 个义项：故事中的人物）；句意是小说里的这位老人是个令人难忘的人物。

senses.title: The qualities of a person
senses.definition: the set of qualities that make a person or place what it is
senses.definitionCN: 使某人或某地成为其自身的全部品质
senses.example: She has a strong character.
senses.exampleCN: 她性格坚强。
senses.why: Greek kharakter was the mark stamped on a coin, an outward sign of what lay inside.
senses.whyCN: 希腊语 kharakter 是压在硬币上的印记，是内在之物的外在标志。

senses.title: A person in a story
senses.definition: a person in a novel, play or film
senses.definitionCN: 小说、戏剧或电影中的人物
senses.example: The old man in the novel is a memorable character.
senses.exampleCN: 小说里的这位老人是个令人难忘的人物。
senses.why: Writers borrowed the stamped mark for the figures stamped into a story.
senses.whyCN: 作家把压印的记号借来，指被压进故事里的那些人物。

senses.title: A letter or symbol
senses.definition: a letter, number or symbol used in writing or printing
senses.definitionCN: 书写或印刷所用的字母、数字或符号
senses.example: The password needs eight characters.
senses.exampleCN: 密码需要八个字符。
senses.why: A stamped mark is literally a written sign, so the alphabet sense is the oldest of all.
senses.whyCN: 压出的印记本就是一种书写符号，所以字符义其实最为古老。

intro.en: Character began as a Greek word for an engraved mark and grew into nature, symbol and story figure.
intro.cn: character 起初是希腊语中「刻痕」的说法，后来生长出本性、符号与故事人物诸义。

items.en: Kharakter meant an engraved mark or stamp.
items.cn: 希腊语 kharakter 意为刻出的痕迹或印章。

items.en: The word also named the distinctive stamp of a person's nature.
items.cn: 该词也指一个人本性上独有的印记。

items.en: Latin character kept both the written sign and the moral sense.
items.cn: 拉丁语 character 同时保留书写符号与品格两义。

items.en: English character first meant a written symbol.
items.cn: 英语 character 最初指书写符号。

items.en: The word now covers personality, reputation and people in fiction.
items.cn: 如今该词涵盖性格、名声与虚构作品中的人物。

note.en: The look-alike group builds on the same stem, while the meaning group lists nature and symbol words.
note.cn: 形近组由同一词干构成，近义组列出本性词与符号词。

entries.definition: a typical feature
to describe the nature of something
more than one character
the pattern of a person's behaviour
entries.definitionCN: 一个人行为的整体模式

entries.definition: a person shown in a story or picture
entries.definitionCN: 故事或图画中出现的人物

entries.definition: a sign that stands for something

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the engraved mark, the Chinese character phrase and the story sense.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子利用刻痕意象、短语 Chinese character 以及故事人物义。

normal.en: Character and carve share the idea of cutting a mark into a surface.
normal.cn: character 与 carve 共享在表面刻下痕迹的意思。

normal.en: A Chinese character is literally a written mark, the oldest sense of the word.
normal.cn: a Chinese character 本就是一个书写记号，正是这个词最古老的义项。

normal.en: In character means the action fits the mark already stamped on the person.
normal.cn: in character 意为行为符合早已印在那人身上的记号。

normal.en: A main character carries the plot, just as a stamp carries a claim.
normal.cn: main character 承载情节，正如印章承载声明。

normal.en: The plural characters covers letters, people and personal traits at once.
normal.cn: 复数 characters 同时涵盖字符、人物与性格特征。

abstract.en: Picture a hot stamp pressed into soft wax.
abstract.cn: 想象一枚滚烫的印章压进软蜡。

abstract.en: Picture a novel where one old man keeps returning.
abstract.cn: 想象一部小说里有一位反复出现的老者。

abstract.en: Picture a password box asking for eight signs.
abstract.cn: 想象一个密码框要求输入八个符号。

examples.en: The town has a character of its own.
examples.cn: 这座小镇自有其特色。

examples.en: The two characters meet again at the end.
examples.cn: 两个人物在结尾重逢。

examples.en: Write your name in capital characters.
examples.cn: 请用大写字母写你的名字。

dict_mnemonic.text: character 与「刻」有关：希腊语原义是刻下的印记，性格就是刻在人身上的记号。

root: 源自希腊语 kharakter（刻痕、印记），经拉丁语 character 进入英语；核心是「刻下的记号」，由此引申出符号、性格与人物。

sensesIntro.en: A stamp makes a written sign, marks a person's nature and presses a figure into a story.
sensesIntro.cn: 一枚印章既留下书写符号，也标记人的本性，还把人物压进故事。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a mark cut into a surface.
core.cn: 核心意象：刻进表面的一个记号。

branches.en: A strong character is the mark of a settled nature.
branches.cn: 坚强的性格是稳定本性的记号。

branches.en: A story character is a figure stamped into fiction.
branches.cn: 故事人物是被压进虚构作品的形象。

branches.en: A character on a screen is the oldest literal sense.
branches.cn: 屏幕上的字符是最古老的字面义。

branches.en: Both senses rest on the idea of a distinguishing mark.
branches.cn: 两个义项都建立在「识别记号」之上。

branches.en: A person's nature and a story figure share one word.
branches.cn: 人的本性与故事人物共用一个词。

intro.en: Character keeps the -character- stem in characteristic, characterize and characterless.
intro.cn: character 在 characteristic、characterize 与 characterless 中保留 -character- 词干。

latinIntro.en: Greek kharakter passed through Latin character into English with the mark intact.
latinIntro.cn: 希腊语 kharakter 经拉丁语 character 进入英语，刻痕意象完好保留。

items.example: Critics characterize the style as spare.
items.exampleCN: 评论家把这种风格描述为简省。

items.meaning: the way a figure is drawn

latinEntries.exampleCN: kharakter 指硬币上的印记。
拉丁语 character 保留了这一记号。

definition_en: a quality that is typical of a person or thing, or being typical of a particular group
core_image: 一个人身上反复出现、可以辨认的记号
scene: 这种鸟的尾羽比身体长得多。A long tail is characteristic of the male bird.
sceneCN: 这里 characteristic 指「特有的；典型的」（第 2 个义项：某类事物明显具有的）；句意是长尾是这种雄鸟的典型特征。

senses.title: A typical feature
senses.definition: a quality that is typical of a person or thing
senses.definitionCN: 某人或某物典型的品质
senses.example: Patience is her best characteristic.
senses.exampleCN: 耐心是她最突出的特点。
senses.why: The Greek adjective meant able to mark, so a characteristic is what marks a thing out.
senses.whyCN: 希腊语形容词意为能留下记号，因此特征是使某物得以辨识的记号。

senses.title: Typical of a group
senses.definition: being a typical quality of a particular person or thing
senses.definitionCN: 属于某人或某物典型性质的
senses.example: A long tail is characteristic of the male bird.
senses.exampleCN: 长尾是这种雄鸟的典型特征。
senses.why: The same adjective says that a mark belongs to a whole kind, not just one member.
senses.whyCN: 同一个形容词说明这个记号属于整个类别，而不只是某一个成员。

intro.en: Characteristic is the Greek adjective of marking, built on the same stem as character.
intro.cn: characteristic 是希腊语中表示「留下记号」的形容词，与 character 同词干。

items.en: Kharakter meant an engraved mark.
items.cn: 希腊语 kharakter 意为刻出的记号。

items.en: Kharakteristikos meant skilled at marking or distinctive.
items.cn: kharakteristikos 意为善于留下记号或有辨识度的。

items.en: Latin character and its adjective passed into scholarly use.
items.cn: 拉丁语 character 及其形容词进入学术用语。

items.en: English characteristic named a distinguishing quality.
items.cn: 十七世纪英语 characteristic 指有区分作用的品质。

items.en: The word now works as both a noun and an adjective.
items.cn: 如今该词既作名词也作形容词。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the character stem, while the meaning group lists feature words.
note.cn: 形近组共享 character 词干，近义组列出表示特征的词。

entries.definition: the nature of a person
to describe the nature of something
in a way that is typical
a noticeable part of something
a particular quality of a person
showing the usual qualities of a group

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the mark root, the phrase be characteristic of and the noun ending -istic.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子利用记号词根、短语 be characteristic of 以及名词化词尾 -istic。

normal.en: Characteristic is the adjective of character, so it describes the mark a thing leaves.
normal.cn: characteristic 是 character 的形容词，因此描述事物留下的记号。

normal.en: Be characteristic of means the quality belongs to the whole kind.
normal.cn: be characteristic of 意为这种品质属于整个类别。

normal.en: A defining characteristic is the mark that decides identity.
normal.cn: a defining characteristic 是决定身份的那道记号。

normal.en: The adverb characteristically adds -ally to the same stem.
normal.cn: 副词 characteristically 是在同一词干后加 -ally。

normal.en: The plural characteristics names several marks at once.
normal.cn: 复数 characteristics 一次指出好几道记号。

abstract.en: Picture a bird with a tail far longer than its body.
abstract.cn: 想象一只尾巴远长于身体的鸟。

abstract.en: Picture a fingerprint that identifies one person only.
abstract.cn: 想象一枚只认出一个人的指纹。

abstract.en: Picture a list of family traits passed down the years.
abstract.cn: 想象一份代代相传的家族特征清单。

examples.en: The two species share several characteristics.
examples.cn: 这两个物种共有若干特征。

examples.en: Patience is characteristic of a good teacher.
examples.cn: 耐心是好老师的典型特征。

examples.en: Her style is characteristic of the period.
examples.cn: 她的风格是那个时期的典型风格。

dict_mnemonic.text: characteristic 是 character 加 -istic：一个人身上反复出现的记号，就是他的特征。

root: 源自希腊语 kharakteristikos（能留下记号的），与 character（刻痕）同词干，经拉丁语进入英语，指有辨识作用的品质。

sensesIntro.en: A mark that identifies a thing gives the noun a feature, and the same mark makes the adjective mean typical.
sensesIntro.cn: 辨识事物的记号给出名词「特征」，同一记号使形容词表示「典型的」。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a mark that tells one kind from another.
core.cn: 核心意象：把一类事物与另一类区分开的记号。

branches.en: Patience as a characteristic is a repeated mark.
branches.cn: 作为特征的耐心是一道反复出现的记号。

branches.en: A long tail marks the whole male group.
branches.cn: 长尾标记出整个雄性群体。

branches.en: Physical characteristics are marks you can observe.
branches.cn: 身体特征是可以观察到的记号。

branches.en: The noun names the mark, the adjective says it fits the kind.
branches.cn: 名词指那道记号，形容词说它契合该类。

branches.en: Be characteristic of links one mark to a whole class.
branches.cn: be characteristic of 把一道记号连到整个类别。

intro.en: Characteristic adds -istic to the character stem, and the adverb adds -ally.
intro.cn: characteristic 在 character 词干后加 -istic，副词再加 -ally。

latinIntro.en: Greek kharakter and kharakteristikos are the mark and the marking adjective.
latinIntro.cn: 希腊语 kharakter 与 kharakteristikos 分别是记号与「留下记号」的形容词。

items.example: The characteristic is easy to see.
items.exampleCN: 这个特征很容易看出来。
寒冷的冬天是该地区的特点。

items.example: The nose is a useful feature.
items.exampleCN: 鼻子是有用的辨识部位。

latinEntries.example: Kharakter is the root of the family.
latinEntries.exampleCN: kharakter 是这一词族的根。

latinEntries.meaningCN: 能留下记号或作区分的
latinEntries.exampleCN: kharakteristikos 演变为 characteristic。

definition_en: to describe the typical qualities of a person or thing, or to be a typical quality of something
core_image: 用几笔勾出一个人最显眼的轮廓
scene: 评论家用一个词概括这座城市的脾气。Critics characterize the city as restless and young.
sceneCN: 这里 characterize 指「把…描绘成」（第 1 个义项：描述某物具有的特征）；句意是评论家把这座城市描绘成躁动而年轻。

senses.title: To describe the nature of
senses.definition: to describe the typical qualities of a person or thing
senses.definitionCN: 描述某人或某物的典型品质
senses.example: Critics characterize the city as restless and young.
senses.exampleCN: 评论家把这座城市描绘成躁动而年轻。
senses.why: The Greek stem meant to stamp a mark, and describing someone is stamping a mark with words.
senses.whyCN: 希腊语词干意为压上记号，而描述一个人就是用词语压上记号。

senses.title: To be a typical mark of
senses.definition: to be a quality that marks a person, place or period
senses.definitionCN: 成为标志某人、某地或某时期的品质
senses.example: Long winters characterize the region.
senses.exampleCN: 漫长的冬天是该地区的特点。
senses.why: The same stamp can be applied by the thing itself, so the verb also means to be the mark.
senses.whyCN: 同一枚印章也可以由事物自己盖上，于是这个动词也表示「就是那道记号」。

intro.en: Characterize adds the verb ending -ize to the Greek mark that gave character.
intro.cn: characterize 在给出 character 的希腊语记号后加上动词词尾 -ize。

items.en: Kharakter meant an engraved mark.
items.cn: 希腊语 kharakter 意为刻出的记号。

items.en: Character kept the sense of a distinctive sign.
items.cn: 拉丁语 character 保留独特记号的含义。

items.en: Caracteriser named the act of marking out a nature.
items.cn: caracteriser 指标示出某种本性的行为。

items.en: English characterize meant to describe the qualities of something.
items.cn: 英语 characterize 意为描述某物的品质。

items.en: The passive be characterized by now names a defining feature.
items.cn: 被动式 be characterized by 如今指某项决定性特征。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the character stem, while the meaning group lists verbs of describing.
note.cn: 形近组共享 character 词干，近义组列出描述类动词。

entries.definition: the nature of a person
a typical feature
described or marked in the past
to say what someone or something is like
entries.definitionCN: 说出某人或某物的样子

entries.definition: to show a person or thing in a certain way
entries.definitionCN: 以某种方式表现人或事物

entries.definition: to state the exact nature of something

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the mark root, the -ize verb ending and the passive pattern be characterized by.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子利用记号词根、-ize 动词词尾以及被动句式 be characterized by。

normal.en: Characterize is character plus -ize, so it means to put the mark into words.
normal.cn: characterize 是 character 加 -ize，意思是用词语把记号说出来。

normal.en: Characterize as is the pattern for calling a thing a certain kind.
normal.cn: characterize as 是把某物称作某种样子的句式。

normal.en: Be characterized by reverses the view and names the mark itself.
normal.cn: be characterized by 把视角反过来，直接说出那道记号。

normal.en: Long winters characterize the region is a natural way to state a feature.
normal.cn: 长冬 characterize the region 是陈述特征的自然说法。

normal.en: The third person characterizes simply adds an s before the z sound.
normal.cn: 第三人称 characterizes 只在 z 音前加一个 s。

abstract.en: Picture a critic drawing three quick lines around a city.
abstract.cn: 想象评论家围着城市飞快画了三笔。

abstract.en: Picture a label being stuck on a whole season.
abstract.cn: 想象一张标签被贴在整个季节上。

abstract.en: Picture a portrait that catches one crooked smile.
abstract.cn: 想象一幅肖像只抓住一个歪嘴的笑。

examples.en: The report characterizes the market as unstable.
examples.cn: 报告把市场描绘成不稳定的。

examples.en: Heavy rain characterizes the summer here.
examples.cn: 大雨是这里夏天的特点。

examples.en: Her work is characterized by sharp detail.
examples.cn: 她的作品以细节锐利为特征。

dict_mnemonic.text: characterize 是 character 加 -ize：把一个人的记号用词语盖出来，就是描绘他的特征。

root: 由 character（希腊语 kharakter，刻痕）加动词后缀 -ize 构成，核心是「压上记号」，引申为描述特征或以…为特征。

sensesIntro.en: Stamping a mark with words gives the describing sense, and being the mark itself gives the passive feature sense.
sensesIntro.cn: 用词语压上记号给出描述义，而自身就是那道记号则给出被动特征义。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a mark pressed onto a person or period.
core.cn: 核心意象：压在人身上或时代上的一个记号。

branches.en: Critics characterize a city by picking a few traits.
branches.cn: 评论家挑出几个特点来描绘一座城市。

branches.en: Long winters mark the whole region.
branches.cn: 漫长的冬天标记出整个地区。

branches.en: Characterize as fits reports and reviews.
branches.cn: characterize as 常见于报告与评论。

branches.en: Active and passive forms share one stamp.
branches.cn: 主动与被动形式共享同一枚印章。

branches.en: Be characterized by names the mark directly.
branches.cn: be characterized by 直接说出那道记号。

intro.en: Characterize combines the character stem with the verb suffix -ize.
intro.cn: characterize 把 character 词干与动词后缀 -ize 结合起来。

latinIntro.en: The stem goes back to Greek kharakter, a mark cut into a surface.
latinIntro.cn: 词干可追溯到希腊语 kharakter，即刻入表面的记号。

items.exampleCN: 这种风格是她作品的特点。

items.example: The age was characterized by speed.
The character of the town changed.

latinEntries.exampleCN: kharakter 给出整个词族。
character 进入法语与英语。

definition_en: to ask a price for goods or services, to accuse someone officially, or to put electrical energy into a battery
core_image: 货物被装上马车，账单也随之压上来
scene: 前台递来一张账单。They charge extra for a room with a view.
sceneCN: 这里 charge 指「收费」（第 1 个义项：为商品或服务索要钱款）；句意是带景观的房间他们要另外收费。

senses.title: To ask for money
senses.definition: to ask a price for goods or services
senses.definitionCN: 为商品或服务索要价款
senses.example: They charge extra for a room with a view.
senses.exampleCN: 带景观的房间他们要另外收费。
senses.why: The Latin verb meant to load a cart, and loading a price onto a bill repeats the same image.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语动词意为往车上装货，把价钱压到账单上重复了同一意象。

senses.title: To accuse formally
senses.definition: to accuse someone officially of a crime or fault
senses.definitionCN: 正式指控某人犯有罪行或过错
senses.example: The police charged him with theft.
senses.exampleCN: 警方指控他盗窃。
senses.why: Blame too could be loaded onto a person, so the cart metaphor gave the legal sense.
senses.whyCN: 罪责也能被压到一个人身上，于是装车的比喻给出了法律义。

senses.title: To put power into a battery
senses.definition: to put electrical energy into a battery or device
senses.definitionCN: 把电能送入电池或设备
senses.example: Charge the phone before the trip.
senses.exampleCN: 出发前把手机充好电。
senses.why: Electricity is loaded into a cell the way goods were loaded into a cart.
senses.whyCN: 电被装进电池，正如货物曾被装进马车。

intro.en: Charge goes back to a Latin verb for loading a cart, and every sense keeps something being loaded.
intro.cn: charge 可追溯到拉丁语表示装车的动词，每个义项都保留「装载某物」的意象。

items.en: Carricare meant to load a wagon or cart.
items.cn: 拉丁语 carricare 意为往货车或马车上装货。

items.en: Caricare extended the verb to loading in general.
items.cn: 晚期拉丁语 caricare 把该动词扩展到一般意义的装载。

items.en: Chargier meant to load, burden or entrust.
items.cn: chargier 意为装载、使负担或托付。

items.en: English charge covered loading, burdening and ordering.
items.cn: 英语 charge 涵盖装载、使负担与命令。

items.en: The word gained the senses of a price, a legal accusation and electric power.
items.cn: 该词获得费用、法律指控与电能等义。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the charge stem, while the meaning group lists accusing and loading words.
note.cn: 形近组共享 charge 词干，近义组列出指控与装载类词。

entries.definition: a device that puts power into a battery
to release or unload something
more than one charge
to say someone has done wrong
to send someone an invoice
to put goods onto a vehicle

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the loading cart, the phrase in charge of and the battery sense.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子利用装货的马车、短语 in charge of 以及电池义。

normal.en: Charge and car share the Latin loading verb, since a cart is what gets loaded.
normal.cn: charge 与 car 共享拉丁语装车动词，因为被装的就是车。

normal.en: In charge of means the duty has been loaded onto you.
normal.cn: in charge of 意为责任被压到了你身上。

normal.en: Charge a fee is loading a price onto the customer.
normal.cn: charge a fee 就是把价钱压到顾客账上。

normal.en: Charge the battery is loading power instead of goods.
normal.cn: charge the battery 是装电而不是装货。

normal.en: Free of charge means no load of cost at all.
normal.cn: free of charge 意为完全不用承担费用的重负。

abstract.en: Picture a cart piled high until the wheels bend.
abstract.cn: 想象一辆车堆得高高的，轮子都压弯了。

abstract.en: Picture a phone plugged in and glowing at the edge.
abstract.cn: 想象一部插着电、边缘发亮的手机。

abstract.en: Picture a guard pointing at a man in a courtroom.
abstract.cn: 想象警卫在法庭上指着一个人。

examples.en: The garage charges too much for repairs.
examples.cn: 这家修车厂收费太高。

examples.en: She was charged with careless driving.
examples.cn: 她被指控粗心驾驶。

examples.en: The nurse in charge of the ward was kind.
examples.cn: 负责病房的护士很和善。

dict_mnemonic.text: charge 与 car 同源：拉丁语原义是往车上装货，装完货就向你收运费。

root: 源自拉丁语 carricare（装车），经晚期拉丁语 caricare 与古法语 chargier 进入英语；由「装载」引申出费用、指控、充电与掌管。

sensesIntro.en: Loading goods gives a price, loading blame gives an accusation, and loading power gives the battery sense.
sensesIntro.cn: 装货给出价钱，装罪责给出指控，装电力给出充电义。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: goods piled onto a cart.
core.cn: 核心意象：货物被堆到马车上。

branches.en: A price is a load placed on the buyer.
branches.cn: 价钱是压在买家身上的一笔负担。

branches.en: An accusation loads blame onto a person.
branches.cn: 指控把罪责压到一个人身上。

branches.en: Charging a battery loads it with power.
branches.cn: 给电池充电就是把电装进去。

branches.en: Money and blame are both burdens carried.
branches.cn: 金钱与罪责都是被背负的重担。

branches.en: The cart image survives in price and power.
branches.cn: 马车意象在价钱与电能中存留。

intro.en: Charge keeps the -charg- stem in charger, discharge and chargeable.
intro.cn: charge 在 charger、discharge 与 chargeable 中保留 -charg- 词干。

latinIntro.en: Latin carricare and Late Latin caricare are the loading verbs behind charge.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 carricare 与晚期拉丁语 caricare 是 charge 背后的「装载」动词。

items.meaning: asked a price in the past
items.exampleCN: 他们向我们收了两次钱。

items.meaning: asking a price or storing power

latinEntries.exampleCN: carricare 演变为 chargier。
caricare 拓宽了词义。

definition_en: kindness shown to others, an organization that helps people in need, or money and goods given to them
core_image: 一只手把面包递到另一只伸出的手里
scene: 教堂门口摆着一只募捐箱。The charity provides meals for homeless families.
sceneCN: 这里 charity 指「慈善机构」（第 2 个义项：从事救济的组织）；句意是这家慈善机构为无家可归的家庭提供餐食。

senses.title: Kindness toward others
senses.definition: kindness and understanding shown to other people
senses.definitionCN: 对他人的善意与体谅
senses.example: She treats everyone with charity.
senses.exampleCN: 她对每个人都心怀善意。
senses.why: Latin caritas meant dearness and Christian love, the warm root of the word.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 caritas 意为珍爱与基督之爱，是这个词温暖的根。

senses.title: An organization that helps
senses.definition: an organization set up to help people in need
senses.definitionCN: 为帮助困难者而设立的组织
senses.example: The charity provides meals for homeless families.
senses.exampleCN: 这家慈善机构为无家可归的家庭提供餐食。
senses.why: A body of people organized for love of neighbours took the name of the love itself.
senses.whyCN: 一群为关爱邻人而组织起来的人，借用了这份关爱本身的名字。

senses.title: Money or aid given
senses.definition: money or goods given to people who need them
senses.definitionCN: 给予困难者的钱款或物品
senses.example: He gave his spare coat to charity.
senses.exampleCN: 他把多余的外套捐给了慈善机构。
senses.why: The abstract love became concrete in the coins and clothes actually handed over.
senses.whyCN: 抽象的仁爱在真正交出的钱币与衣物中变得具体。

intro.en: Charity descends from a Latin word for dearness, which early Christian writers used for love of one's neighbours.
intro.cn: charity 源自拉丁语表示珍爱的词，早期基督教作家用它指对邻人的爱。

items.en: Carus meant dear or precious.
items.cn: 拉丁语 carus 意为珍贵的、亲爱的。

items.en: Caritas meant dearness and, in Christian use, loving kindness.
items.cn: caritas 意为珍爱，在基督教用法中指仁爱。

items.en: Charité carried both love and almsgiving.
items.cn: charité 同时带有爱与施舍之意。

items.en: English charity named Christian love and mercy.
items.cn: 英语 charity 指基督之爱与怜悯。

items.en: The word now also names the groups and gifts that express this love.
items.cn: 如今该词也指表达这份爱的组织与捐赠。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the charitable stem, while the meaning group lists kindness and aid words.
note.cn: 形近组共享 charitable 词干，近义组列出善意与援助类词。

entries.definition: generous in giving help
in a kind and generous way
more than one charity
the quality of being friendly and caring
help given to those in need
money given to a good cause

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the dear root, the charity shop phrase and the gift sense.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子利用「珍爱」词根、短语 charity shop 以及捐赠义。

normal.en: Charity and cherish both come from a Latin word for something dear.
normal.cn: charity 与 cherish 都来自拉丁语中表示珍贵之物的词。

normal.en: A charity shop turns donated things into money for the poor.
normal.cn: charity shop 把捐赠物变成给穷人的钱。

normal.en: Out of charity means the act comes from kindness, not duty.
normal.cn: out of charity 意为出于善心而非义务。

normal.en: Charity begins at home is the proverb that keeps the word warm.
normal.cn: Charity begins at home 这句谚语让这个词保持温度。

normal.en: The plural charities covers several organizations at once.
normal.cn: 复数 charities 一次指好几家机构。

abstract.en: Picture a hand passing bread through a narrow doorway.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手从窄门口递出面包。

abstract.en: Picture a collection box heavy with small coins.
abstract.cn: 想象一只装满零钱的募捐箱。

abstract.en: Picture a shop window full of second-hand coats.
abstract.cn: 想象一扇摆满旧外套的商店橱窗。

examples.en: The concert raised money for local charities.
examples.cn: 音乐会为当地慈善机构筹款。

examples.en: He never speaks of anyone without charity.
examples.cn: 他谈起任何人都带着善意。

examples.en: The old books were sold for charity.
examples.cn: 那些旧书被卖掉用于慈善。

dict_mnemonic.text: charity 与 cherish 同源：心里珍爱一个人，才会伸手施舍，这就是慈善。

root: 源自拉丁语 carus（珍贵的）及其派生 caritas（珍爱、仁爱），经古法语 charité 进入英语；与 cherish 同源。

sensesIntro.en: Dearness becomes Christian love, love becomes an organized body, and the body turns into gifts of money and goods.
sensesIntro.cn: 珍爱变成基督之爱，爱变成有组织的团体，团体再化为钱物捐赠。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: love that reaches out to a neighbour.
core.cn: 核心意象：伸向邻人的那份爱。

branches.en: Treating people with charity is the oldest sense.
branches.cn: 以善意待人是最古老的义项。

branches.en: A charity is a body organized around that love.
branches.cn: 慈善机构是围绕这份爱组织起来的团体。

branches.en: Giving to charity turns feeling into goods.
branches.cn: 捐给慈善把情感变成实物。

branches.en: Both senses keep the idea of giving freely.
branches.cn: 两个义项都保留自愿给予的意思。

branches.en: Organizations and gifts depend on each other.
branches.cn: 机构与捐赠彼此依存。

intro.en: Charity keeps the car- dear root in charitable and charitably.
intro.cn: charity 在 charitable 与 charitably 中保留 car-「珍爱」词根。

latinIntro.en: Latin carus and caritas are the dear thing and the love that produced charity.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 carus 与 caritas 是产出 charity 的「珍贵之物」与「爱」。

items.exampleCN: 两家慈善机构分享了这笔基金。

latinEntries.example: Carus is the root of charity.
latinEntries.exampleCN: carus 是 charity 的词根。
caritas 给出法语 charité。

definition_en: a drawing that shows information as lines or figures, a detailed map of the sea, or to record how something develops
core_image: 一张画满曲线与刻度的纸
scene: 墙上挂着一张起伏的折线图。The chart shows sales rising since spring.
sceneCN: 这里 chart 指「图表」（第 1 个义项：用线条或图形表示数据）；句意是图表显示销售额自春天以来不断上升。

senses.title: A diagram of data
senses.definition: a drawing that shows information as lines, bars or figures
senses.definitionCN: 用线条、条形或图形展示信息的图
senses.example: The chart shows sales rising since spring.
senses.exampleCN: 图表显示销售额自春天以来不断上升。
senses.why: A written sheet was used to plot numbers, and the sheet gave its name to the picture.
senses.whyCN: 人们用纸页来标画数字，纸页便把名字给了这幅图。

senses.title: A map of the sea
senses.definition: a detailed map of an area of sea and its coasts
senses.definitionCN: 某片海域及其海岸的详细地图
senses.example: The captain studied the chart before dark.
senses.exampleCN: 船长在天黑前研究了海图。
senses.why: The oldest charts were sheets of paper marked with coasts and depths for sailors.
senses.whyCN: 最古老的 chart 就是画着海岸与水深、供水手使用的纸页。

senses.title: To record how something develops
senses.definition: to record or follow the progress of something over time
senses.definitionCN: 记录或跟踪某事物随时间的发展
senses.example: The doctor charted her recovery week by week.
senses.exampleCN: 医生逐周记录她的康复情况。
senses.why: Plotting points on a paper chart became a verb for watching any course.
senses.whyCN: 在纸图上标点，变成了观察任何进程的动词。

intro.en: Chart comes from a Greek word for a sheet of papyrus, which became paper, map and finally diagram.
intro.cn: chart 源自希腊语表示纸莎草纸页的词，后来依次变成纸、地图，最后指图表。

items.en: Chartes meant a sheet of papyrus for writing.
items.cn: 希腊语 chartes 意为供书写的纸莎草纸页。

items.en: Carta meant paper or a written document.
items.cn: 拉丁语 carta 意为纸或书面文件。

items.en: Charte named a document and later a sea map.
items.cn: charte 指文件，后指海图。

items.en: English chart first meant a sea map for navigation.
items.cn: 英语 chart 最初指导航用的海图。

items.en: The word now chiefly means a diagram of information.
items.cn: 如今该词主要指展示信息的图表。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the carta root, while the meaning group lists graphs and maps.
note.cn: 形近组共享 carta 词根，近义组列出图表与地图类词。

entries.definition: a formal document granting rights
recorded or mapped in the past
not yet mapped or explored
a diagram of numerical relations
a simple drawing of how something works
entries.definitionCN: 说明事物如何运作的简图

entries.definition: a drawing of an area of land

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the paper root, the bar chart phrase and the sea map sense.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子利用「纸」词根、短语 bar chart 以及海图义。

normal.en: Chart, card and charter all come from Latin carta, a sheet of paper.
normal.cn: chart、card 与 charter 都来自拉丁语 carta，即一张纸。

normal.en: A bar chart turns numbers into paper bars you can compare.
normal.cn: bar chart 把数字变成可以比较的纸上长条。

normal.en: A sea chart is the oldest kind, drawn for sailors.
normal.cn: 海图是最古老的一种，为水手而画。

normal.en: To chart progress is to draw the course on paper.
normal.cn: chart progress 就是把进程画在纸上。

normal.en: Off the chart means the value has gone past every marked line.
normal.cn: off the chart 意为数值越过了所有标出的线。

abstract.en: Picture a line climbing steeply across squared paper.
abstract.cn: 想象一条线在方格纸上陡峭上升。

abstract.en: Picture a captain tracing depths with one finger.
abstract.cn: 想象船长用一根手指描着水深。

abstract.en: Picture a wall of weather symbols pinned to a board.
abstract.cn: 想象一墙钉在板上的天气符号。

examples.en: The pie chart divides spending into four parts.
examples.cn: 饼图把开销分成四部分。

examples.en: Sailors once depended on hand-drawn charts.
examples.cn: 水手曾依赖手绘海图。

examples.en: The team charted the river's course last summer.
examples.cn: 团队去年夏天绘制了这条河的走向。

dict_mnemonic.text: chart 与 card 同源：都来自拉丁语「纸」（carta），纸上画满线就成了图表。

root: 源自希腊语 chartes（纸莎草纸页），经拉丁语 carta 与古法语 charte 进入英语；与 card、charter 同源。

sensesIntro.en: A sheet of paper first holds a sea map, then a diagram, and finally the verb of plotting any course.
sensesIntro.cn: 一张纸先承载海图，再承载图表，最后化为标画任何进程的动词。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a marked sheet of paper.
core.cn: 核心意象：一张画满记号的纸。

branches.en: A bar chart is data drawn on paper.
branches.cn: 条形图是画在纸上的数据。

branches.en: A sea chart guides a ship past hidden rocks.
branches.cn: 海图引导船只避开暗礁。

branches.en: To chart a recovery is to mark each step.
branches.cn: 记录康复就是标出每一步。

branches.en: Both are sheets marked to guide the eye.
branches.cn: 两者都是为引导视线而标记的纸页。

branches.en: The mapped route becomes the recorded course.
branches.cn: 绘出的路线变成被记录的进程。

intro.en: Chart keeps the cart- paper root in uncharted and chartless.
intro.cn: chart 在 uncharted 与 chartless 中保留 cart-「纸」词根。

latinIntro.en: Greek chartes and Latin carta are the papyrus sheet and the paper behind the word.
latinIntro.cn: 希腊语 chartes 与拉丁语 carta 是这个词背后的纸莎草纸页与纸张。

items.example: The chart is out of date.

items.meaning: mapped or recorded in the past

items.exampleCN: 小船进入未标注的水域。
他们没有海图就出航了。

latinEntries.exampleCN: chartes 指书写用纸。
carta 给出 chart 与 charter。

definition_en: to run after a person or animal in order to catch them, or to try hard to obtain something
core_image: 一个人沿着地上的脚印拼命奔跑
scene: 狗从院门冲出去追一只野兔。The dog chased a rabbit across the field.
sceneCN: 这里 chase 指「追赶」（第 1 个义项：追着某人或某物跑）；句意是狗追着一只野兔跑过田野。

senses.title: To run after someone
senses.definition: to run after a person or animal in order to catch them
senses.definitionCN: 追在人或动物后面以便抓住
senses.example: The dog chased a rabbit across the field.
senses.exampleCN: 狗追着一只野兔跑过田野。
senses.why: The Latin verb meant to try to seize, and running after prey is that attempt in motion.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语动词意为试图抓住，追着猎物跑正是这种企图在移动。

senses.title: To try to obtain something
senses.definition: to try hard to get something such as money, success or a person
senses.definitionCN: 努力获得金钱、成功或某个人
senses.example: He spent years chasing a dream.
senses.exampleCN: 他花了多年追求一个梦想。
senses.why: The hunt for prey became a hunt for goals that cannot be caught by hand.
senses.whyCN: 对猎物的追捕，变成了对手无法用手抓住的目标的追逐。

senses.title: An act of pursuing
senses.definition: the act of running after someone or something
senses.definitionCN: 追在某人或某物后面的行为
senses.example: The police gave up the chase.
senses.exampleCN: 警方放弃了追逐。
senses.why: The verb's action turned into a noun, so the pursuit itself became a chase.
senses.whyCN: 动词的动作转成名词，追逐本身便成了一个 chase。

intro.en: Chase comes from a Latin verb of trying to seize, through Old French chacier.
intro.cn: chase 源自拉丁语表示试图抓住的动词，经古法语 chacier 传来。

items.en: Captare meant to try to catch or seize.
items.cn: 拉丁语 captare 意为试图抓住或夺取。

items.en: Captiare carried the hunting sense into popular speech.
items.cn: 晚期拉丁语 captiare 把追猎义带入日常口语。

items.en: Chacier meant to hunt or drive away.
items.cn: chacier 意为追猎或赶走。

items.en: English chase first meant to hunt animals.
items.cn: 英语 chase 最初指追猎动物。

items.en: The word now covers car chases and the pursuit of aims.
items.cn: 如今该词涵盖汽车追逐与对目标的追求。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the chase stem, while the meaning group lists pursuing verbs.
note.cn: 形近组共享 chase 词干，近义组列出追捕类动词。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the seize root, the car chase phrase and the pursuit of a dream.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子利用「抓住」词根、短语 car chase 以及追梦义。

normal.en: Chase and catch share an old idea of seizing, since one leads to the other.
normal.cn: chase 与 catch 共享古老的「抓住」之意，因为前者通向后者。

normal.en: Chase after is the phrase for both a runaway dog and a distant goal.
normal.cn: chase after 既用于跑掉的狗，也用于遥远的目标。

normal.en: Give chase means to start running after, not to hand something over.
normal.cn: give chase 意为开始追赶，而不是把东西交出去。

normal.en: Chase away reverses the direction and means to drive off.
normal.cn: chase away 把方向反过来，意为赶走。

normal.en: A car chase fills the screen with motion and noise.
normal.cn: car chase 用动作与噪声填满银幕。

abstract.en: Picture a dog cutting a straight line through tall grass.
abstract.cn: 想象一只狗在深草中划出一条直线。

abstract.en: Picture a runner reaching for a finish line that keeps moving.
abstract.cn: 想象跑者伸手去够一条不断移动的终点线。

abstract.en: Picture two cars flashing through a wet tunnel.
abstract.cn: 想象两辆车在潮湿的隧道里飞驰。

examples.en: The cat chased the ball under the sofa.
examples.cn: 猫把球追到了沙发底下。

examples.en: Reporters chased the story for weeks.
examples.cn: 记者追这条新闻追了好几周。

examples.en: He gave up the chase after two blocks.
examples.cn: 他追了两条街就放弃了。

dict_mnemonic.text: chase 与 catch 同源感：追（chase）的最终目的，就是抓（catch）到。

root: 源自拉丁语 captare（试图抓住），经晚期拉丁语 captiare 与古法语 chacier 进入英语；与 catch 同源。

sensesIntro.en: Trying to seize gives the physical pursuit, then the pursuit of aims, then the name of the pursuit itself.
sensesIntro.cn: 试图抓住先给出身体上的追赶，再给出对目标的追求，最后给出追逐这一行为本身。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a runner closing in on prey.
core.cn: 核心意象：奔跑者逐渐逼近猎物。

branches.en: A dog chases a rabbit to catch it.
branches.cn: 狗追野兔是为了抓住它。

branches.en: A dream is chased without any physical prey.
branches.cn: 追梦并没有实体的猎物。

branches.en: The chase itself becomes a thing to name.
branches.cn: 追逐本身成了一个可以被命名的东西。

branches.en: The verb and noun describe one continuous action.
branches.cn: 动词与名词描述同一个连续动作。

branches.en: Prey and goals are both things to run after.
branches.cn: 猎物与目标都是要追的东西。

intro.en: Chase forms chaser and chasing, and the collocation chase away reverses the direction.
intro.cn: chase 构成 chaser 与 chasing，搭配 chase away 则把方向反过来。

latinIntro.en: Latin captare is the seizing verb behind chase and catch.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 captare 是 chase 与 catch 背后的「抓取」动词。

items.example: The film has two long chases.
items.exampleCN: 这部电影有两段长长的追逐戏。

items.example: Captare is the old hunting verb.
items.exampleCN: captare 是古老的追猎动词。

items.meaning: to follow in order to reach
items.exampleCN: 他们继续推进这个计划。

latinEntries.exampleCN: captare 给出法语 chacier。
chacier 以 chase 进入英语。

definition_en: to talk in a friendly and informal way, or a friendly informal conversation
core_image: 两个人隔着桌子随意地说笑
scene: 午后咖啡馆里两个人低声说话。They sat and chatted for an hour.
sceneCN: 这里 chat 指「聊天」（第 1 个义项：轻松随意地交谈）；句意是他们坐着聊了一个小时。

senses.title: To talk casually
senses.definition: to talk in a friendly and informal way
senses.definitionCN: 以友好而随意的方式交谈
senses.example: They sat and chatted for an hour.
senses.exampleCN: 他们坐着聊了一个小时。
senses.why: Chat is a shortened chatter, the sound of quick light talk.
senses.whyCN: chat 是 chatter 的缩短，后者指轻快话语的声音。

senses.title: A friendly conversation
senses.definition: a friendly and informal conversation
senses.definitionCN: 友好而随意的谈话
senses.example: We had a long chat about old school days.
senses.exampleCN: 我们聊了很久学生时代的旧事。
senses.why: The action of chatting became a countable thing, so one talk is one chat.
senses.whyCN: 聊天的动作变成可数之物，于是一次谈话就是一次 chat。

senses.title: To exchange messages online
senses.definition: to exchange short messages with people on the internet
senses.definitionCN: 在互联网上与人互发短消息
senses.example: She chats with friends every evening.
senses.exampleCN: 她每晚都和朋友网上聊天。
senses.why: The same easy talk moved from a table to a screen and kept its name.
senses.whyCN: 同样轻松的谈话从桌边移到屏幕上，名字保持不变。

intro.en: Chat began as a short form of chatter, the quick sound of idle talk.
intro.cn: chat 起初是 chatter 的缩短形式，即闲话轻快的声音。

items.en: Chatteren meant to talk quickly and idly.
items.cn: 中古英语 chateren 意为快速而闲散地说话。

items.en: Chat shortened the verb and kept the friendly tone.
items.cn: chat 缩短了这个动词，并保留友善的语气。

items.en: The noun chat named a light conversation.
items.cn: 名词 chat 指轻松的谈话。

items.en: Chat room and online chat extended the word to screens.
items.cn: chat room 与 online chat 把该词扩展到屏幕上。

items.en: The word now covers both spoken and typed small talk.
items.cn: 如今该词既指口头闲谈，也指打字聊天。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the chatter stem, while the meaning group lists talk words.
note.cn: 形近组共享 chatter 词干，近义组列出谈话类词。

entries.definition: fond of talking
to talk quickly about small things
more than one chat
to speak with someone
a talk between people
talk about other people's lives

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the chatter root, the phrase have a chat and the online chat sense.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子利用 chatter 词根、短语 have a chat 以及网上聊天义。

normal.en: Chat is chatter with the end cut off, just as the talk is light and short.
normal.cn: chat 是砍掉尾巴的 chatter，正如这种谈话轻而短。

normal.en: Have a chat turns the verb into a countable meeting.
normal.cn: have a chat 把动词变成一次可数的会面。

normal.en: Chat about is the pattern for naming the topic.
normal.cn: chat about 是说出话题的句式。

normal.en: An online chat happens without any sound at all.
normal.cn: online chat 完全没有声音。

normal.en: The adjective chatty describes a person who chats easily.
normal.cn: 形容词 chatty 形容容易聊起来的人。

abstract.en: Picture two cups cooling on a table between two talkers.
abstract.cn: 想象两个说话人之间，桌上两只杯子慢慢变凉。

abstract.en: Picture a phone screen filling with short grey bubbles.
abstract.cn: 想象手机屏幕被短短的灰色气泡填满。

abstract.en: Picture a group laughing at the door of a shop.
abstract.cn: 想象一群人在店门口说笑。

examples.en: We chatted about the match on the way home.
examples.cn: 回家路上我们聊了那场比赛。

examples.en: Come in for a chat when you have time.
examples.cn: 有时间进来聊聊天。

examples.en: He spends the evening chatting with friends online.
examples.cn: 他整晚都在网上和朋友聊天。

dict_mnemonic.text: chat 就是 chatter 的缩短：话多而轻松，正是聊天的样子。

root: 由中古英语 chatteren（快速闲谈）缩短而来，原为拟声词，模拟轻快话语的声音，后指轻松的交谈。

sensesIntro.en: Quick idle sound becomes the act of talking, then one conversation, then typed talk on a screen.
sensesIntro.cn: 轻快的闲话声先变成交谈动作，再变成一次谈话，最后变成屏幕上的打字交谈。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two people talking easily with no purpose.
core.cn: 核心意象：两个人没有目的地轻松交谈。

branches.en: To chat is to talk without a fixed aim.
branches.cn: 聊天就是没有固定目的地说话。

branches.en: A chat is one such talk, countable and short.
branches.cn: a chat 是其中一次谈话，可数而短小。

branches.en: Online chat moves the same ease onto a screen.
branches.cn: 网上聊天把同样的轻松移到屏幕上。

branches.en: The verb and noun share one friendly tone.
branches.cn: 动词与名词共享同一种友善语气。

branches.en: Spoken and typed chats both build contact.
branches.cn: 口头与打字聊天都在建立联系。

intro.en: Chat forms chatty and chatter, and doubles its final t before -ed and -ing.
intro.cn: chat 构成 chatty 与 chatter，并在 -ed 与 -ing 前双写词尾 t。

latinIntro.en: The word is native English, echoing the sound of quick talk rather than a Latin root.
latinIntro.cn: 该词是英语本土词，模拟快速说话的声音，而非来自拉丁词根。

items.exampleCN: 孩子们叽叽喳喳说个不停。

definition_en: costing little money, or low in price because of poor quality
core_image: 市场上挂着一块写着低价的旧木牌
scene: 夜市摊位上的衣服标价很低。The market sells cheap clothes and warm soup.
sceneCN: 这里 cheap 指「便宜的」（第 1 个义项：价格低的）；句意是这个市场卖便宜衣服和热汤。

senses.title: Costing little money
senses.definition: costing little money, or less than you expected
senses.definitionCN: 花费很少，或低于预期的价格
senses.example: The market sells cheap clothes and warm soup.
senses.exampleCN: 这个市场卖便宜衣服和热汤。
senses.why: Old English ceap meant a bargain, and a good bargain is simply a low price.
senses.whyCN: 古英语 ceap 意为划算的交易，而划算的交易就是低价钱。

senses.title: Of poor quality
senses.definition: low in price because of poor quality or workmanship
senses.definitionCN: 因质量或做工差而价格低廉
senses.example: The handle broke; it was a cheap tool.
senses.exampleCN: 把手断了，这是件劣质工具。
senses.why: Goods sold too far below the usual price came to be judged as poorly made.
senses.whyCN: 卖得远低于常价的货物，渐渐被判断为做工粗劣。

intro.en: Cheap comes from an Old English word for trade and bargain, and only later meant a low price.
intro.cn: cheap 源自古英语表示交易与划算的词，后来才指低价钱。

items.en: Ceap meant a bargain, a purchase or trade.
items.cn: 古英语 ceap 意为划算的交易、购买或买卖。

items.en: Chep appeared in phrases naming a market or a good buy.
items.cn: chep 出现在指市场或划算买卖的短语中。

items.en: Cheap came to mean low in price.
items.cn: cheap 转而表示价格低。

items.en: The word also began to suggest poor quality.
items.cn: 该词也开始带有质量低劣的暗示。

items.en: Cheap now describes both a bargain and something shoddy.
items.cn: 如今 cheap 既形容划算，也形容粗劣。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the trader root, while the meaning group lists price words.
note.cn: 形近组共享商人词根，近义组列出价格类词。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the bargain root, the phrase dirt cheap and the quality sense.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子利用「交易」词根、短语 dirt cheap 以及质量义。

normal.en: Cheap and chapman share the Old English word for trade.
normal.cn: cheap 与 chapman 共享古英语中表示交易的词。

normal.en: A cheap price began as the price of a good bargain.
normal.cn: 便宜的价格起初就是一笔划算交易的价格。

normal.en: Dirt cheap means the price is as low as the ground.
normal.cn: dirt cheap 意为价钱低到贴近地面。

normal.en: A cheap trick costs little and deserves little respect.
normal.cn: a cheap trick 代价很小，也不值得尊重。

normal.en: The comparative cheaper and the superlative cheapest double nothing and add -er and -est.
normal.cn: 比较级 cheaper 与最高级 cheapest 不双写词尾，只加 -er 与 -est。

abstract.en: Picture a hand-written price tag swinging in the wind.
abstract.cn: 想象一张手写价签在风里摇晃。

abstract.en: Picture a stall piled with folded shirts at dusk.
abstract.cn: 想象黄昏时堆满分叠衬衫的摊位。

abstract.en: Picture a handle snapping off on the first day.
abstract.cn: 想象把手在第一天就断了。

examples.en: The tickets are cheaper if you book early.
examples.cn: 早点订票会便宜些。

examples.en: This is the cheapest room in the hotel.
examples.cn: 这是旅馆里最便宜的房间。

examples.en: Cheap materials rarely last long.
examples.cn: 劣质材料很少能用得久。

dict_mnemonic.text: cheap 与 chapman 同源：古英语 ceap 是交易，交易先讲价钱，后来就指便宜。

root: 源自古英语 ceap（交易、划算的买卖），与 chapman（商人）同源；词义由「划算」转为「价格低」，再引申出「低劣」。

sensesIntro.en: A bargain gives the low price, and goods priced far below the norm give the poor quality sense.
sensesIntro.cn: 划算的交易给出低价义，远低于常价的货物则给出低劣义。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a price tag set far below the usual mark.
core.cn: 核心意象：一张远低于常价的价签。

branches.en: Cheap clothes cost little money.
branches.cn: 便宜衣服花费很少。

branches.en: A cheap tool breaks because it was poorly made.
branches.cn: 劣质工具因做工差而断裂。

branches.en: The phrase on the cheap names the low-cost route.
branches.cn: on the cheap 指低成本的途径。

branches.en: Low price and low quality often travel together.
branches.cn: 低价与低质常常同行。

branches.en: A cheap trick is shoddy in a moral sense.
branches.cn: a cheap trick 在道德意义上也很粗劣。

intro.en: Cheap forms cheaper, cheapest, cheaply, cheapness and cheapen with common endings.
intro.cn: cheap 借助常见词尾构成 cheaper、cheapest、cheaply、cheapness 与 cheapen。

latinIntro.en: The word is native English; Old English ceap is the trade word behind the family.
latinIntro.cn: 该词是英语本土词，古英语 ceap 是这一词族背后的交易词。

items.exampleCN: 劣质仿品贬低了这一设计。

items.example: Ceap is the old trade word.

definition_en: to act dishonestly in order to gain an advantage, or a person who does this
core_image: 考场上把答案写在小纸条上的人
scene: 考场里静得能听见笔尖沙沙作响。He tried to cheat in the final exam and was caught at once.
sceneCN: 这里 cheat 指「作弊」（第 1 个义项：在考试或比赛中用不正当手段取胜）；句意是他想在期末考试中作弊，当场就被抓住了。

senses.title: To trick someone for gain
senses.definition: to make someone believe something false so that you gain money or an advantage
senses.definitionCN: 让人相信假事，从而骗取钱财或好处
senses.example: The seller cheated an old couple out of their savings.
senses.exampleCN: 卖家骗走了一对老夫妇的积蓄。
senses.why: The old legal word for seizing property gave the idea of taking by unfair means.
senses.whyCN: 古老的法律用语本指夺取财产，由此生出用不正当手段取得的意思。

senses.title: To act dishonestly in a test
senses.definition: to break the rules of an exam or a game in order to do better
senses.definitionCN: 为取得更好成绩而违反考试或比赛规则
senses.example: Two students were caught cheating in the midterm.
senses.exampleCN: 两名学生在期中考试中被发现作弊。
senses.why: The general sense of unfair gain narrowed to unfair gain inside a contest.
senses.whyCN: 一般意义上的不义之财缩小为比赛内部的不正当获利。

senses.title: A dishonest person
senses.definition: a person who deceives others, or a single act of deception
senses.definitionCN: 欺骗他人的人，也指一次欺骗行为
senses.example: He turned out to be a cheat who sold fake tickets.
senses.exampleCN: 原来他是个卖假票的骗子。
senses.why: English often turns an action verb into a noun that names the person who does it.
senses.whyCN: 英语常把动作动词转成名词，用来指做这件事的人。

intro.en: Cheat is a worn-down legal word that once meant land falling back to a lord.
intro.cn: cheat 是一个磨短的法律词，原本指归回领主的土地。

items.en: Excadere meant to fall out or fall away.
items.cn: 拉丁语 excadere 意为脱落、掉出。

items.en: Excadere named property that fell back to a lord for want of heirs.
items.cn: 该词在中世纪拉丁语中指因无继承人而归回领主的财产。

items.en: Escheat carried that legal sense into French.
items.cn: escheat 把这个法律含义带进法语。

items.en: The shortened form cheat first meant to seize property by such a claim.
items.cn: 缩略形式 cheat 最初指以这类名目夺取财产。

items.en: The sense widened to any dishonest gain, then to a dishonest person.
items.cn: 词义扩展到一切不义之财，再转指行骗的人。

note.en: The look-alike group keeps a short similar spelling, while the meaning group names acts of dishonesty.
note.cn: 形近组共享相近的短拼写，近义组列出各种不诚实的行为。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the cheap look-alike, the old escheat and the three fixed prepositions.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子利用形近词 cheap、古词 escheat 以及三个固定介词。

normal.en: Cheat and cheap differ by one letter: a cheat sells you something cheap and fake.
normal.cn: cheat 与 cheap 只差一个字母：骗子卖给你便宜却虚假的东西。

normal.en: The old word escheat meant land falling back to a lord; cheat is that word worn down.
normal.cn: 古词 escheat 指土地归回领主，cheat 就是它磨短后的样子。

normal.en: Cheat in an exam, cheat at cards, cheat on a test: each preposition marks its own scene.
normal.cn: cheat in an exam、cheat at cards、cheat on a test，每个介词都标出自己的场景。

normal.en: A cheat is a person and cheating is the act, while cheater is the plain agent noun.
normal.cn: a cheat 指人，cheating 指行为，cheater 则是最直白的施动名词。

normal.en: Cheat death is the one flattering phrase: it means to escape death narrowly.
normal.cn: cheat death 是唯一带褒义的搭配，意为死里逃生。

abstract.en: Picture a corner of a small answer note slipping out of a sleeve.
abstract.cn: 想象一小角答案纸条从袖口滑出来。

abstract.en: Picture a hand swapping one card under a card table.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手在牌桌下换掉一张牌。

abstract.en: Picture a man whispering low prices for fake tickets at a station gate.
abstract.cn: 想象一个男人在车站门口低声兜售假票。

examples.en: He cheated the company out of a large sum.
examples.cn: 他骗走了公司一大笔钱。

examples.en: The teacher warned us never to cheat.
examples.cn: 老师警告我们绝不要作弊。

examples.en: A cheat never keeps friends for long.
examples.cn: 骗子留不住朋友。

dict_mnemonic.text: cheat 与 cheap 只差一个字母：便宜货里最容易藏着骗局。

root: 源自拉丁语 excadere（脱落），经中世纪拉丁语与古法语 escheat（无嗣归公的土地）缩略为 cheat，本指以不正当名目取得财产。

sensesIntro.en: The seizure of property gives the general sense of dishonest gain, which narrows to exam rooms and then shifts to the person.
sensesIntro.cn: 对财产的夺取给出「不义之财」的总义，随后缩小到考场，最后转到行骗的人。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hand hiding an answer note inside a sleeve.
core.cn: 核心意象：把答案纸条藏在袖子里的那只手。

branches.en: A seller takes money by telling a lie.
branches.cn: 卖家靠说谎拿走钱财。

branches.en: The exam room is where the unfair gain happens.
branches.cn: 考场是不正当获利发生的场所。

branches.en: The same word then names the person who lies.
branches.cn: 同一个词随后指说谎的那个人。

branches.en: Both senses share the idea of a hidden unfair move.
branches.cn: 两个义项都共享「暗中不正当操作」的意思。

branches.en: Cheating in a test earns the label cheat.
branches.cn: 在考试中作弊就会得到 cheat 这个称呼。

intro.en: One short root serves the verb, the noun and every derived form of cheat.
intro.cn: 一个短词根支撑 cheat 的动词、名词与全部派生形式。

latinIntro.en: Latin excadere and Old French escheat stand behind the modern word.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 excadere 与古法语 escheat 是现代这个词的前身。

items.example: They cheated on the last quiz.
The cheated buyers sued the shop.
items.exampleCN: 受骗的买家起诉了这家店。

items.example: Escheat was a medieval legal term.
items.exampleCN: escheat 是中世纪的法律术语。

latinEntries.meaning: to fall out or fall away
latinEntries.example: Excadere is the remote base of cheat.
latinEntries.exampleCN: excadere 是 cheat 的远源词基。

latinEntries.meaning: property falling back to a lord
latinEntries.example: Escheat lost its first sound to become cheat.
latinEntries.exampleCN: escheat 丢掉首音后变成 cheat。

definition_en: to examine something to make sure it is correct or safe, or an examination of this kind
core_image: 拿着一份清单逐项打勾的手
scene: 出发前屋里还亮着灯。She checked the list twice before leaving the house.
sceneCN: 这里 check 指「核对」（第 1 个义项：逐项查看是否正确）；句意是她出门前把清单核对了两遍。

senses.title: To examine and confirm
senses.definition: to look at something carefully in order to see whether it is correct or safe
senses.definitionCN: 仔细查看某物，判断其是否正确或安全
senses.example: Please check your answers before handing in the paper.
senses.exampleCN: 交卷之前请核对你的答案。
senses.why: A chess warning asked a player to look at the board at once, and looking closely became the core sense.
senses.whyCN: 棋盘上的警告要求棋手立刻查看局势，仔细查看便成了核心义。

senses.title: To stop or slow something
senses.definition: to stop or slow the progress of something harmful
senses.definitionCN: 阻止或减缓有害事物的发展
senses.example: The new rules are meant to check the spread of the fire.
senses.exampleCN: 新规定旨在阻止火势蔓延。
senses.why: Blocking the king in chess turned into the general idea of holding something back.
senses.whyCN: 在国际象棋中挡住国王，转化为一般意义上的「拦住」。

senses.title: A bank order
senses.definition: a printed order telling a bank to pay money from an account
senses.definitionCN: 指示银行从账户付款的印刷单据
senses.example: He paid the rent by check.
senses.exampleCN: 他用支票付了房租。
senses.why: The word also named a written order that could be checked against a bank account.
senses.whyCN: 这个词也指可向银行账户核对兑现的书面命令。

intro.en: Check began as the chess cry that warned a king he was in danger.
intro.cn: check 最初是国际象棋里提醒国王处境危险的一声喊。

items.en: Shah meant king.
items.cn: 波斯语 shah 意为国王。

items.en: The cry al-shah warned that the king was threatened.
items.cn: 阿拉伯语中的喊声提示国王受到威胁。

items.en: Eschec named the chess move that attacked the king.
items.cn: 古法语 eschec 指攻击国王的那一步棋。

items.en: English check first meant a chess threat to the king.
items.cn: 英语 check 最初指棋局中对国王的威胁。

items.en: The word widened to any sudden stop, then to inspection and to a bank order.
items.cn: 词义扩展到任何突然的制止，再扩展到查看与银行票据。

note.en: The look-alike group differs by one sound or one letter, while the meaning group lists acts of careful looking.
note.cn: 形近组只差一个音或一个字母，近义组列出仔细查看的动作。

entries.definition: a bank order spelled the British way
entries.definitionCN: 英式拼写的银行付款单

entries.definition: the side of the face below the eye
a board game of kings and queens
entries.definitionCN: 以国王与王后为棋子的棋盘游戏

entries.definition: to look at something in detail
to look at something officially for faults
to prove that something is true

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the chess origin, three everyday phrases with check and the British spelling cheque.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子利用国际象棋来源、三个含 check 的日常搭配以及英式拼写 cheque。

normal.en: The chess word check shouted that a king was in danger, and English kept the shout.
normal.cn: 国际象棋里的 check 高喊国王有危险，英语把这声喊留了下来。

normal.en: Check the list, check in, check out: three daily phrases all involve confirming something.
normal.cn: check the list、check in、check out，三个日常搭配都涉及确认。

normal.en: Cheque is the British spelling of the same sound, used only for the bank order.
normal.cn: cheque 是同一读音的英式拼写，只用于银行付款单。

normal.en: To check a fire is to hold it back, the old chess sense of blocking a king.
normal.cn: to check a fire 是把火拦住，正是旧日棋局中挡住国王的意思。

normal.en: Checklist and check-in are compounds built directly from the verb stem.
normal.cn: checklist 与 check-in 都是直接从动词词干构成的复合词。

abstract.en: Picture a finger moving down a paper list, ticking one line at a time.
abstract.cn: 想象一根手指沿纸上的清单下移，一行行打勾。

abstract.en: Picture a chess piece halted just before it reaches the king.
abstract.cn: 想象一枚棋子冲到国王面前却被挡住。

abstract.en: Picture a bank clerk sliding a printed slip across a counter.
abstract.cn: 想象银行职员把一张印刷单据从柜台推过来。

examples.en: She checked the door twice before going to bed.
examples.cn: 她睡前把门检查了两遍。

examples.en: The doctor will check your eyes tomorrow.
examples.cn: 医生明天会检查你的眼睛。

examples.en: A firm answer can check a rumour at once.
examples.cn: 坚定的答复能立刻止住谣言。

dict_mnemonic.text: check 与 chess 同源：棋盘上一声「将军」，就是把对方的行动拦下来。

root: 源自波斯语 shah（国王），经阿拉伯语与古法语 eschec 进入英语，本为国际象棋中「将军」的警告声。

sensesIntro.en: The warning cry gives the idea of a sudden stop, which splits into careful looking and into holding something back.
sensesIntro.cn: 警告的喊声给出「突然制止」的意思，随后分出仔细查看与加以拦阻两条线。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a voice calling out that the king must be watched.
core.cn: 核心意象：一声喊出「看好国王」的提醒。

branches.en: Looking closely grew out of the demand to watch the board.
branches.cn: 仔细查看源自「看好棋盘」的要求。

branches.en: Stopping a fire repeats the old blocking move.
branches.cn: 阻止火势沿用了旧日拦挡的动作。

branches.en: A bank order is checked against an account before it is paid.
branches.cn: 银行票据付款前要对着账户核对。

branches.en: Both senses keep the energy of a sudden halt.
branches.cn: 两个义项都保留了「骤然停住」的力度。

branches.en: Inspection and the paper order share one written word.
branches.cn: 查看与纸质票据共用一个书写形式。

intro.en: Check stays a single short stem across its verb, noun and compound forms.
intro.cn: check 在动词、名词与复合形式中始终保持同一个短词干。

latinIntro.en: The stem reaches back through Old French eschec to Persian shah, the word for a king.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词干经古法语 eschec 上溯到波斯语 shah，即国王。

items.example: She is checking the list now.
The pilot ran through the checklist.

items.exampleCN: 检查员发现了一个错误。

items.meaning: the act of registering on arrival

items.example: She wrote a cheque for the rent.
items.exampleCN: 她开了一张付房租的支票。

latinEntries.meaning: the chess threat to a king
latinEntries.exampleCN: eschec 进入英语后写作 check。

latinEntries.example: Shah is the oldest layer of check.
latinEntries.exampleCN: shah 是 check 最古老的一层。

definition_en: the soft side of the face below the eye, or bold rudeness that shows no shame
core_image: 笑起来鼓起的两侧脸颊
scene: 屋里忽然安静下来，孩子低着头。A tear ran down her cheek when she heard the news.
sceneCN: 这里 cheek 指「脸颊」（第 1 个义项：眼睛下方的面部侧面）；句意是她听到消息时一滴泪顺着脸颊流了下来。

collocations.zh: 挨了打还把另一边脸转过去

senses.title: The side of the face
senses.definition: the soft part of the face on either side below the eye
senses.definitionCN: 眼睛下方脸两侧柔软的部分
senses.example: A tear rolled down his cheek.
senses.exampleCN: 一滴泪顺着他的脸颊滚落。
senses.why: Old English used the word for the jaw, and the meaning later moved to the soft side of the face.
senses.whyCN: 古英语用这个词指颌骨，后来意义移到面部柔软的一侧。

senses.title: Bold rudeness
senses.definition: rude boldness that shows no shame or respect
senses.definitionCN: 毫无羞耻与敬意的放肆无礼
senses.example: He had the cheek to ask for more money.
senses.exampleCN: 他竟然有脸再要钱。
senses.why: A person without shame does not blush, so the word for the face came to mean impudence.
senses.whyCN: 不知羞耻的人不会脸红，于是表示「脸」的词也用来表示放肆。

intro.en: Cheek began as a word for the jaw and slid upward to the soft side of the face.
intro.cn: cheek 起初指颌骨，后来向上移到面部柔软的一侧。

items.en: A root kau- named the jaw and the act of chewing.
items.cn: 日耳曼语词根 kau- 指颌骨与咀嚼的动作。

items.en: Ceace named the jaw and the bony side of the face.
items.cn: 古英语 ceace 指颌骨与面部骨性的一侧。

items.en: Cheke shifted to the soft flesh below the eye.
items.cn: cheke 的意义移到眼睛下方的柔软皮肉。

items.en: The word gained a second sense of bold rudeness.
items.cn: 这个词获得了「放肆无礼」的第二个义项。

items.en: Cheek now covers anatomy, manners and many fixed phrases.
items.cn: 如今 cheek 涵盖身体部位、举止以及大量固定搭配。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the same opening sound, while the meaning group names the face and boldness.
note.cn: 形近组共享相同的开头音，近义组列出面部与放肆的说法。

entries.definition: to examine something closely
a solid food made from milk
entries.definitionCN: 用牛奶制成的固体食物

entries.definition: low in price or poor in quality
either of the bones that hold the teeth
boldness that others find rude
entries.definitionCN: 被别人视为无礼的大胆

entries.definition: fearless rudeness

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the jaw root, the chewing link and the idiom about turning the other cheek.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子利用颌骨词根、咀嚼联系以及「转过另一边脸」的习语。

normal.en: Cheek once meant jaw, and the jaw muscle moves whenever you chew.
normal.cn: cheek 曾指颌骨，而咀嚼时动的正是颌部的肌肉。

normal.en: The plural cheeks simply adds an s to the soft side of the face.
normal.cn: 复数 cheeks 只是在表示面颊的词后加 s。

normal.en: Turn the other cheek is the famous phrase: it means to answer harm with patience.
normal.cn: turn the other cheek 是著名说法，意为以忍耐回应伤害。

normal.en: Cheek to cheek describes two dancers held close together.
normal.cn: cheek to cheek 形容两个舞者贴得很近。

normal.en: The same word turns abstract in have the cheek, which means to be boldly rude.
normal.cn: 同一个词在 have the cheek 中变得抽象，意为厚着脸皮。

abstract.en: Picture two red patches on a child's face after a long run.
abstract.cn: 想象孩子长跑之后脸上两团红。

abstract.en: Picture a tear stopping halfway down a still face.
abstract.cn: 想象一滴泪停在静止的脸颊中间。

abstract.en: Picture someone smiling calmly after being refused twice.
abstract.cn: 想象某人被拒绝两次后仍平静地笑着。

examples.en: Her cheeks went red when the teacher praised her.
examples.cn: 老师表扬她时，她的脸颊红了。

examples.en: He kissed his mother on the cheek and left.
examples.cn: 他亲了亲母亲的脸颊就走了。

examples.en: She had the cheek to blame the whole team.
examples.cn: 她竟有脸把责任推给整个团队。

dict_mnemonic.text: cheek 与 chew 同源：咀嚼时一鼓一鼓的地方，就是脸颊。

root: 源自日耳曼语词根 kau-（颌骨、咀嚼），古英语作 ceace，中古英语 cheke 转指眼睛下方的面颊。

sensesIntro.en: The jaw word climbs to the soft side of the face, and from the face it reaches the idea of shameless boldness.
sensesIntro.cn: 表示颌骨的词上移到面部柔软处，再由「脸」引申出不知羞耻的放肆。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: the soft curve of a face beside the smile.
core.cn: 核心意象：笑容旁边那一道柔软的脸部弧线。

branches.en: The physical cheek sits below the eye.
branches.cn: 实体的脸颊位于眼睛下方。

branches.en: The abstract sense names bold disrespect.
branches.cn: 抽象义指大胆无礼。

branches.en: Kissing on the cheek marks affection.
branches.cn: 亲脸颊表示亲近。

branches.en: The face word lends itself to idioms about shame.
branches.cn: 表示脸的词自然延伸出关于羞耻的习语。

branches.en: Having the cheek means lacking all shame.
branches.cn: have the cheek 意为毫无羞耻。

intro.en: Cheek builds a small family from one Old English stem.
intro.cn: cheek 由一个古英语词干构成一个小词族。

latinIntro.en: The stem is Germanic rather than Latin, and it links to the word for chewing.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词干属日耳曼语而非拉丁语，并与表示咀嚼的词相连。

items.example: Her cheek was warm to the touch.
items.exampleCN: 她的脸颊摸上去是温的。

items.example: His cheeks were red from the cold.

items.exampleCN: 那个调皮的男孩顶了嘴。

items.meaning: in a rude but playful way
items.example: He grinned cheekily at the guard.

items.meaning: to crush food with the teeth

latinEntries.example: Ceace is the oldest recorded form of cheek.
latinEntries.exampleCN: ceace 是 cheek 有记录的最古形式。

definition_en: a solid food made from milk and pressed into blocks or wheels
core_image: 一块切开、露出小孔的黄色奶酪
scene: 面包刚出炉，桌上摆着一小盘切好的奶酪。He cut a thin slice of cheese for the child.
sceneCN: 这里 cheese 指「奶酪」（第 1 个义项：用牛奶制成的固体食品）；句意是他给孩子切了一薄片奶酪。

senses.title: The dairy food
senses.definition: a solid food made from milk and pressed into blocks or wheels
senses.definitionCN: 用牛奶制成、压成块或轮的固体食品
senses.example: This cheese is made from goat's milk.
senses.exampleCN: 这种奶酪是用羊奶做的。
senses.why: The word came straight from Latin caseus, the name of the food itself.
senses.whyCN: 这个词直接来自拉丁语 caseus，正是这种食物本身的名称。

senses.title: The photographer's call
senses.definition: a word said to make people smile before a photograph is taken
senses.definitionCN: 拍照前让人露出笑容时喊的口令
senses.example: The photographer asked us to say cheese.
senses.exampleCN: 摄影师让我们喊「茄子」。
senses.why: The long vowel forces the mouth into a smile, so the food word became a studio call.
senses.whyCN: 长元音迫使嘴形拉成微笑，于是这个食物词成了摄影棚里的口令。

intro.en: Cheese is one of the oldest Latin loanwords in English, taken from caseus.
intro.cn: cheese 是英语中最古老的拉丁语借词之一，来自 caseus。

items.en: Caseus named cheese.
items.cn: 拉丁语 caseus 指奶酪。

items.en: West Germanic speakers borrowed the word as kasjus.
items.cn: 西日耳曼语使用者把它借入，作 kasjus。

items.en: Cese named the food on the table.
items.cn: 古英语 cese 指桌上的这种食物。

items.en: The spelling settled as chese and then cheese.
items.cn: 拼写先固定为 chese，后又变成 cheese。

items.en: The word now names hundreds of kinds and also the call for a smile.
items.cn: 如今这个词指数百个品种，也指拍照时的微笑口令。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the same opening sound, while the meaning group lists other dairy foods.
note.cn: 形近组共享相同的开头音，近义组列出其他奶制品。

entries.definition: a board game of kings and queens
entries.definitionCN: 以国王与王后为棋子的棋盘游戏

entries.definition: the side of the face below the eye
to run after someone quickly
a soft yellow food made from cream
entries.definitionCN: 用奶油制成的黄色软食

entries.definition: a thick food made from fermented milk
entries.definitionCN: 用发酵牛奶制成的浓稠食品

entries.definition: the thick fatty part of milk
entries.definitionCN: 牛奶中浓稠含脂的部分

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the Latin source, the shape of the food and the photographer's call.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子利用拉丁语来源、食物形状以及拍照口令。

normal.en: Cheese and casein share a root: casein is the milk protein that makes cheese firm.
normal.cn: cheese 与 casein 同根：酪蛋白正是让奶酪变硬的那种牛奶蛋白。

normal.en: Say cheese: the long vowel pulls the mouth into a smile.
normal.cn: say cheese：长元音把嘴角拉成一个笑。

normal.en: Cheese is usually uncountable, but cheeses means several kinds.
normal.cn: cheese 通常不可数，而 cheeses 指好几个品种。

normal.en: Cheesy first meant like cheese, then came to mean cheap and sentimental.
normal.cn: cheesy 先指「像奶酪的」，后来指廉价而煽情。

normal.en: Cheeseburger and cheesecake are compounds that keep the food word whole.
normal.cn: cheeseburger 与 cheesecake 都是保留食物原词的复合词。

abstract.en: Picture a yellow wheel of cheese with one wedge removed.
abstract.cn: 想象一只黄色奶酪轮被切走一角。

abstract.en: Picture a knife pulling a thin slice away from a block.
abstract.cn: 想象刀从整块奶酪上片下薄薄一片。

abstract.en: Picture a family holding a smile while a camera clicks.
abstract.cn: 想象一家人保持笑容，相机咔嚓一响。

examples.en: Cheese is made by curdling milk.
examples.cn: 奶酪是通过让牛奶凝结制成的。

examples.en: He bought three kinds of cheese for the party.
examples.cn: 他为聚会买了三种奶酪。

examples.en: The children shouted cheese as the camera flashed.
examples.cn: 相机闪光时孩子们喊着「茄子」。

dict_mnemonic.text: cheese 与 chess 只差一个字母：棋盘旁的桌子上，常摆着一块奶酪。

root: 源自拉丁语 caseus（奶酪），由西日耳曼语借入，古英语作 cese，中古英语拼作 chese。

sensesIntro.en: The food sense is the original one, and the studio call grew out of the shape the word forces on the mouth.
sensesIntro.cn: 食物义是最初的义项，摄影口令则由这个词逼出的嘴形发展而来。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a pressed block of milk turned solid and yellow.
core.cn: 核心意象：一块被压紧、凝成固体的黄色奶块。

senses.exampleCN: 这位化学家发表了一篇关于新型聚合物的论文。
senses.why: The -ist ending marks a person who practises the science named by the stem.

senses.title: The makeup of a substance
senses.definition: the chemical composition or behaviour of a material

senses.exampleCN: 泄漏之后湖水的化学成分发生了变化。

senses.whyCN: 这门科学的名称被用来指它所测量的那些性质本身。

senses.title: Mutual understanding

definition_en: a printed order telling a bank to pay a sum of money from an account
core_image: 一张写着金额并签了名的纸条
scene: 柜台前的队伍慢慢往前挪。He wrote a cheque for the full amount and handed it over.
sceneCN: 这里 cheque 指「支票」（第 1 个义项：指示银行付款的票据）；句意是他开了一张全额支票并递了过去。

senses.title: A written bank order
senses.definition: a printed form on which you write a sum and sign your name so that a bank pays that money
senses.definitionCN: 印好格式、由你填写金额并签名，让银行付出这笔钱的单据
senses.example: She paid the plumber by cheque.
senses.exampleCN: 她用支票付了水管工的钱。
senses.why: The word is a later spelling of check, fixed when the bank sense needed its own written form.
senses.whyCN: 这个词是 check 后来的拼写，在银行义需要独立书写形式时固定下来。

senses.title: Freedom to act at will
senses.definition: permission to act freely, as if given a cheque with the amount left empty
senses.definitionCN: 像拿到一张金额空着的支票那样被允许自由行动
senses.example: The board gave the new director a blank cheque.
senses.exampleCN: 董事会给了新主管一张「空白支票」。
senses.why: A blank cheque lets the holder fill in any sum, so the phrase came to mean unlimited freedom.
senses.whyCN: 空白支票允许持有人填任何金额，于是这个说法表示不受限的自由。

intro.en: Cheque is the same word as check, respelled to keep the bank sense apart.
intro.cn: cheque 与 check 本是同一个词，改拼是为了把银行义区分出来。

items.en: Shah meant king.
items.cn: 波斯语 shah 意为国王。

items.en: Eschec named the chess move that threatened the king.
items.cn: 古法语 eschec 指威胁国王的那一步棋。

items.en: Check first meant a chess threat.
items.cn: 英语 check 最初指棋局中的威胁。

items.en: Check also named a written order on a bank.
items.cn: check 也用来指对银行开出的书面付款命令。

items.en: British banks fixed the spelling cheque for the money sense.
items.cn: 英国银行把表示钱的这一义项固定拼作 cheque。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the same sound, while the meaning group names other written orders for money.
note.cn: 形近组读音相同，近义组列出其他书面的付款凭证。

entries.definition: to examine, or the American spelling of a bank order
entries.definitionCN: 检查，或支票的美式拼写

entries.definition: the side of the face below the eye
a board game of kings and queens
entries.definitionCN: 以国王与王后为棋子的棋盘游戏

entries.definition: a written order for payment by a bank
entries.definitionCN: 银行开具的书面付款命令

entries.definition: a printed paper that can be exchanged for goods
entries.definitionCN: 可换取商品的印刷凭据

entries.definition: a paper showing money owed for goods

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the shared sound with check, the chess history and the blank cheque idiom.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子利用与 check 相同的读音、国际象棋来源以及空白支票的习语。

normal.en: Cheque and check sound alike because they are one word with two spellings.
normal.cn: cheque 与 check 读音相同，因为它们是同一个词的两种拼写。

normal.en: The British write cheque for money and check for inspection.
normal.cn: 英国人用 cheque 表示钱，用 check 表示检查。

normal.en: The chess word check hides inside cheque: a bank order also says stop and pay.
normal.cn: 棋盘上的 check 藏在 cheque 里：一张支票也在说「停，付钱」。

normal.en: A blank cheque has an empty amount, so it stands for unlimited freedom.
normal.cn: 空白支票金额空着，因此表示不受限制的自由。

normal.en: Chequebook and cheque card are the two everyday compounds.
normal.cn: chequebook 与 cheque card 是两个日常复合词。

abstract.en: Picture a pen filling in an amount on a printed slip.
abstract.cn: 想象一支笔在印刷单据上填金额。

abstract.en: Picture a signature drying at the bottom of a paper.
abstract.cn: 想象纸底的签名正在变干。

abstract.en: Picture a bank clerk stamping a slip and sliding it back.
abstract.cn: 想象银行职员盖章后把单据推回来。

examples.en: He wrote a cheque for two hundred pounds.
examples.cn: 他开了一张两百英镑的支票。

examples.en: Most shops no longer accept payment by cheque.
examples.cn: 多数商店不再接受支票付款。

examples.en: The committee handed the designer a blank cheque.
examples.cn: 委员会给了设计师全权委托。

dict_mnemonic.text: cheque 就是 check 的英式写法：把「检查」换成「付款单」，读音一点没变。

root: 与 check 同源，出自波斯语 shah（国王）、古法语 eschec（将军），十九世纪英国银行为付款票据固定拼作 cheque。

sensesIntro.en: The bank order is the literal sense, and the empty amount on a blank cheque gives the figurative sense of free action.
sensesIntro.cn: 银行付款单是字面义，空白支票上金额的空缺给出自由行动的比喻义。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a signed slip that turns paper into money.
core.cn: 核心意象：一张签了名、把纸变成钱的单据。

branches.en: The literal sense is a payment order.
branches.cn: 字面义项是付款命令。

branches.en: The figurative sense is unlimited permission.
branches.cn: 比喻义项是不受限制的许可。

branches.en: The plural cheques counts single slips.
branches.cn: 复数 cheques 用来数一张张单据。

branches.en: Both senses rest on the same printed form.
branches.cn: 两个义项都依托同一张印刷单据。

branches.en: A blank cheque is signed but left empty.
branches.cn: 空白支票签了名却空着金额。

intro.en: Cheque keeps the short check stem in a British spelling.
intro.cn: cheque 以英式拼写保留 check 这个短词干。

latinIntro.en: The stem is not Latin at all; it reaches Persian shah through Old French eschec.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词干并非拉丁语，而是经古法语 eschec 上溯波斯语 shah。
