items.meaning: the chess threat to a king
items.exampleCN: eschec 是两种拼写共同的源头。

latinEntries.meaning: a chess threat to the king
latinEntries.example: Eschec became English check and cheque.
latinEntries.exampleCN: eschec 变成英语的 check 与 cheque。

definition_zh: 樱桃；樱桃树；樱桃色；樱桃木
definition_en: a small round red or dark red fruit with a single hard stone, or the tree that bears it
core_image: 枝头垂着的小红果，咬开是甜汁和一枚硬核
scene: 初夏的果园里，孩子们踮起脚尖伸手去够枝头最红的那一颗。She picked the ripest cherry from the tree and ate it on the spot.
sceneCN: 这里 cherry 是「樱桃」（第 1 个义项：樱桃树的果实）；句意是「她从树上摘下最熟的那颗樱桃，当场吃了」。

pos.zh: 樱桃；樱桃树；樱桃木；樱桃色

derivatives.zh: 由 cherry（樱桃）加 pick（挑选）构成，义为「挑肥拣瘦，只挑最好的」
由 cherry-pick 加表示工具的 -er 构成，义为「（高空作业用的）升降台，原指摘樱桃车」

senses.title: The edible fruit of the cherry tree
senses.definition: a small round fruit with red or dark red skin, sweet or sour flesh, and a single hard stone
senses.definitionCN: 一种小圆果，皮呈红色或深红，果肉甜或酸，中间有一枚硬核
senses.example: The cake was topped with cream and a single cherry.
senses.exampleCN: 蛋糕上点缀着奶油和一颗樱桃。
senses.why: The word names the fruit itself, so the core image is the round red berry hanging on the branch.
senses.whyCN: 这个词最早指的就是果实本身，核心意象是挂在枝头的小红果。

senses.title: The tree that bears cherries
senses.definition: the tree (genus Prunus) that produces cherries, grown for fruit or for blossom
senses.definitionCN: 结樱桃的树（李属），种来收果或赏花
senses.example: They planted a cherry in the garden years ago.
senses.exampleCN: 多年前他们在花园里种了一棵樱桃树。
senses.why: English routinely extends fruit names to the plant itself, so the berry image grows into the tree.
senses.whyCN: 英语习惯把果名直接延伸到果树本身，果实意象便扩展成整棵树。

senses.title: The wood of the cherry tree
senses.definition: the reddish-brown timber of the cherry tree, valued for furniture and cabinets
senses.definitionCN: 樱桃树的木材，呈红棕色，常用于做家具和柜子
senses.example: The cabinet is made of solid cherry.
senses.exampleCN: 这个柜子是实心樱桃木做的。
senses.why: Material names in English often come from the tree source, extending the image from fruit to timber.
senses.whyCN: 英语里木材名常直接取自树名，意象从果实延伸到木材。

senses.title: A bright red colour like a cherry
senses.definition: a bright red colour resembling ripe cherries, often used of lips, paint or fabrics
senses.definitionCN: 像熟樱桃一样的鲜红色，常用来形容嘴唇、油漆或布料
senses.example: Her new scarf was a glossy cherry.
senses.exampleCN: 她的新围巾是亮泽的樱桃红色。
senses.why: The intense red skin of the fruit becomes a colour name, a common path in colour vocabulary.
senses.whyCN: 果实鲜红的果皮被借为颜色名，这是颜色词汇最常见的形成路径。

senses.title: The hymen, in informal or euphemistic use
senses.definition: in informal slang, virginity, especially in the phrase to lose one's cherry
senses.definitionCN: 在俚语中委婉指童贞，常见于 lose one's cherry 一语
senses.example: That slang sense appears mainly in very informal speech.
senses.exampleCN: 这个俚语义主要出现在非常口语的场合。
senses.why: The round red shape invites euphemistic slang, a figurative leap from fruit to taboo topic.
senses.whyCN: 红圆的果形引发了委婉俚语，从果实意象跳跃到禁忌话题。

senses.title: The best part or prize, in figurative use
senses.titleCN: 精华；最好的部分（比喻用法）
senses.definition: figuratively, the best or most attractive thing, as in the cherry on the cake
senses.definitionCN: 比喻最精彩、最诱人的部分，如 the cherry on the cake（锦上添花之物）
senses.example: Winning the award was the cherry on top of a great season.
senses.exampleCN: 获奖是精彩赛季锦上添花的一笔。
senses.why: The sweet red fruit placed on top of a dessert stands for the finishing touch, hence the best part.
senses.whyCN: 甜点顶端那颗红樱桃象征点睛之笔，由此引申为最好的部分。

intro.en: Cherry is one of the many fruit words English borrowed through French from Latin, and the singular form was reshaped by folk etymology.
intro.cn: cherry 是英语经法语借自拉丁语的众多果名之一，其单数形式还曾被民间词源重新塑造。

items.en: Latin had cerasus (or ceresium), the cherry tree and its fruit, borrowed from Greek kerasos; the ultimate source is possibly an Anatolian language, though this is generally considered uncertain.
items.cn: 拉丁语有 cerasus（或 ceresium），指樱桃树及其果实，借自希腊语 kerasos；更早的来源一般认为不确定，可能出自安纳托利亚语系语言。

items.en: Latin cerasum evolved into Old French cerise, which Anglo-Norman speakers brought to England after 1066.
items.cn: 拉丁语 cerasum 演变为古法语 cerise，1066 年之后随盎格鲁-诺曼人带入英格兰。

items.en: The word appears in Middle English as cherise or cheryse; because the final s was heard as a plural ending, speakers cut it off and the singular cherry was formed by mistake, a classic folk etymology.
items.cn: 中古英语写作 cherise / cheryse；词尾的 s 被误当成复数标记，人们把它剪掉，错误地造出了单数 cherry，是典型的民间词源现象。

items.en: The plural cherries was re-formed from the new singular, and the tree sense and the timber sense became established as English gardeners and cabinetmakers used the word daily.
items.cn: 复数 cherries 从新的单数重新生成，果树义和木材义随着园丁和木匠的日常使用而固定下来。

items.en: Colour names, figurative phrases such as the cherry on the cake, and the compound cherry-pick all grew from the fruit image.
items.cn: 颜色名、the cherry on the cake 等比喻短语，以及复合词 cherry-pick，都是从果实意象生长出来的。

note.en: Cherry belongs to a small family of fruit-and-tree words, and it is easy to confuse with visually similar English words.
note.cn: cherry 属于一小组「果实＋树木」词，也容易和拼写或发音相近的英语词混淆。

entries.definition: to love and care for something deeply
entries.definitionCN: 珍爱；珍视——开头字母与 cherry 相同，但词源无关，只是拼写相近

entries.definition: happy and cheerful in manner
entries.definitionCN: 欢快的；兴致高的——与 cherry 仅一个字母之差，词源不同

entries.definition: a bright red colour, borrowed directly from French
entries.definitionCN: 樱桃红——cherry 的古法语前身 cerise 直接借入英语成为颜色词

entries.definition: a small juicy fruit without a stone, such as a strawberry or blueberry
entries.definitionCN: 浆果——同为小型果实，但 berry 无硬核，cherry 有核

entries.definition: a soft round fruit with yellow-pink skin and a large stone
entries.definitionCN: 桃——同为核果，果形更大，也常进入比喻用法

entries.definition: a juicy oval fruit with a single stone, purple or red when ripe
entries.definitionCN: 李子——同属李属核果，与樱桃亲缘关系很近

normalIntro.en: Use the word's shape, sound and word family to lock it in.
normalIntro.cn: 用词形、读音和词族把 cherry 牢牢记住。

normal.en: cherry ends in -erry like berry and merry, a rhyming trio of small happy words.
normal.cn: cherry 词尾 -erry 与 berry（浆果）、merry（欢乐）押韵，三个轻快的小词一组。

normal.en: Old French cerise lost its s because English heard it as a plural, so cherry is cerise minus the mistaken ending.
normal.cn: 古法语 cerise 的 s 被误当复数剪掉，cherry 就是「cerise 去掉错认的词尾」。

normal.en: Plural cherries changes y to i before -es, the same spelling rule as babies and cities.
normal.cn: 复数 cherries 把 y 变 i 再加 es，规则同 babies、cities。

normal.en: Cherry blossom is the famous spring image; the tree sense lives in this phrase.
normal.cn: cherry blossom（樱花）是著名的春日意象，树的义项就藏在这个短语里。

normal.en: Cherry-pick means to take only the best, the fruit picked by hand.
normal.cn: cherry-pick 意为「只挑最好的」，即亲手摘果的意象。

abstract.en: Picture a tiny red globe with a green stem, the exact image the word carries.
abstract.cn: 想一颗带绿梗的小红球，这正是这个词的核心画面。

abstract.en: See a cake crowned by one cherry: the finishing touch, the best part.
abstract.cn: 看蛋糕顶上那颗樱桃：点睛之笔，最好的部分。

abstract.en: Hear the rhyme cherry–berry–merry as three stones skipping on water.
abstract.cn: 把 cherry–berry–merry 的韵脚想象成水上连跳的三颗小石子。

examples.en: She picked the ripest cherry from the tree and ate it on the spot.
examples.cn: 她从树上摘下最熟的那颗樱桃，当场吃了。

examples.en: The avenue is lined with cherry trees that bloom in April.
examples.cn: 街道两旁种着四月开花的樱桃树。

examples.en: Being named captain was the cherry on top of a perfect season.
examples.cn: 被任命为队长是完美赛季锦上添花的一笔。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「拆粒」——把枝头的小红果一颗颗拆下来吃，一拆一粒，就是 cherry（樱桃）。

root: 一般认为源自拉丁语 cerasus（樱桃树／樱桃），经古法语 cerise 进入英语；拉丁语词又借自希腊语 kerasos，更早来源可能出自安纳托利亚地区的语言，具体存疑。英语把词尾 s 误当复数剪掉，形成单数 cherry，属民间词源。与 cher只是词源同源，与 cherish、cheery 仅拼写相近。

sensesIntro.en: From the fruit itself, the word spreads naturally to the tree, its timber, its colour, and then into slang and figurative uses.
sensesIntro.cn: 从果实本身出发，词义自然扩展到樱桃树、樱桃木、樱桃红色，再进入俚语和比喻用法。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a small round red fruit with one hard stone hanging from a branch
core.cn: 核心意象：枝头垂着的一颗小圆红果，咬开有一枚硬核

branches.en: the fruit itself, eaten fresh or as dessert topping
branches.cn: 果实本身，鲜食或作甜点缀

branches.en: the tree that bears the fruit, from orchard to blossom
branches.cn: 结出果实的樱桃树，从果园到樱花

branches.en: the wood and the colour both borrowed from the fruit's appearance
branches.cn: 木材与颜色都借自果实的外观

branches.en: slang euphemism grown from the fruit's shape
branches.cn: 由果形引出的俚语委婉用法

branches.en: figurative use: the cherry on top as the best part
branches.cn: 比喻用法：顶上那颗樱桃即最好的部分

intro.en: Cherry is a simple loanword rather than a built-up derivative, so its affix notes focus on the French source, its colour relative, and the compounds it has formed in English.
intro.cn: cherry 是单纯借词而非层层派生的产物，构词说明聚焦法语来源、同源颜色词，以及它在英语中形成的复合词。

latinIntro.en: The Latin ancestor cerasus left a few descendants in European languages; the clearest relative in English is cerise.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语祖源 cerasus 在欧洲各语言留下少量后裔，英语中最清晰的同源词是 cerise。

items.meaningCN: 樱桃树；樱桃（拉丁语源头词）
items.example: Latin cerasus came from Greek kerasos.
items.exampleCN: 拉丁语 cerasus 借自希腊语 kerasos。

items.meaningCN: 樱桃树（希腊语中介来源）
items.example: Greek kerasos is the direct source of the Latin word.

items.structure: Old French noun, borrowed into English
items.meaningCN: 樱桃红；樱桃（古法语原形）

items.meaning: the flowers of the cherry tree

items.example: A cherry tree stood by the gate.

items.meaning: to choose only the best or most profitable items
items.example: Critics accused the report of cherry-picking data.
items.exampleCN: 批评者指责该报告挑拣数据。

items.meaning: a bright red like ripe cherries
items.example: The car was painted cherry red.

items.meaning: a tart variety of cherry used in cooking
items.example: The pie is made with sour cherries.
items.exampleCN: 这个派是用酸樱桃做的。

definition_en: the front part of the body between the neck and the stomach, or a large strong box with a lid
core_image: 一只带铜锁的木箱，也指人的胸腔
scene: 阁楼里堆着落满灰的旧物。She found a wooden chest full of letters under the window.
sceneCN: 这里 chest 指「箱子」（第 2 个义项：带盖的大型储物箱）；句意是她在窗下找到一只装满信件的木箱。

collocations.phrase: fold one's arms across one's chest

derivatives.zh: 胸部不适的；胸部突出的

senses.title: The front of the body
senses.definition: the front part of the body between the neck and the stomach
senses.definitionCN: 脖子与腹部之间的身体前部
senses.example: He felt a sharp pain in his chest.
senses.exampleCN: 他感到胸口一阵剧痛。
senses.why: The box word was applied to the rib cage, which encloses the heart and lungs like a lid.
senses.whyCN: 表示箱子的词被用到肋骨构成的「胸腔」上，因为它像带盖的容器一样包住心肺。

senses.title: A large strong box
senses.definition: a large strong box with a lid, used for storing things
senses.definitionCN: 带盖的大型坚固储物箱
senses.example: The sailors kept their clothes in a wooden chest.
senses.exampleCN: 水手们把衣服放在一只木箱里。
senses.why: The oldest sense came from Greek and Latin words for a box.
senses.whyCN: 最古老的义项来自希腊语与拉丁语中表示箱子的词。

senses.title: A piece of furniture with drawers
senses.definition: a piece of furniture with drawers, used for keeping clothes
senses.definitionCN: 带抽屉、用来存放衣物的家具
senses.example: The clean shirts are in the chest of drawers.
senses.exampleCN: 干净的衬衫在五斗柜里。
senses.why: A chest of drawers is a box turned into furniture, so the short name stayed.
senses.whyCN: 五斗柜是把箱子变成家具，简短的名称便保留下来。

intro.en: Chest first meant a box, and only later borrowed the shape for the human rib cage.
intro.cn: chest 最初指箱子，后来才借这个形状指人的胸腔。

items.en: Kiste named a box for storage.
items.cn: 希腊语 kiste 指储物的箱子。

items.en: Cista named a box or a case.
items.cn: 拉丁语 cista 指箱子或匣子。

items.en: Cest named a box with a lid.
items.cn: 古英语 cest 指带盖的箱子。

items.en: The box word was transferred to the rib cage.
items.cn: 表示箱子的词被转用到肋骨围成的胸腔上。

items.en: Chest covers the body, storage boxes and chests of drawers.
items.cn: 如今 chest 涵盖身体部位、储物箱与五斗柜。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the ch- opening, while the meaning group lists containers and body words.
note.cn: 形近组共享 ch- 开头，近义组列出容器与身体部位词。

entries.definition: a board game of kings and queens
entries.definitionCN: 以国王与王后为棋子的棋盘游戏

entries.definition: the side of the face below the eye
a solid food made from milk
entries.definitionCN: 用牛奶制成的固体食品

entries.definition: a container with stiff sides and a lid
a large strong case for travel
a container made for one kind of thing
entries.definitionCN: 为某类物品制作的容器

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the box origin, the container shape of the body and the drawers idiom.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子利用「箱子」来源、身体的容器形状以及五斗柜的说法。

normal.en: Chest began as a box, and the ribs still make a box around the heart.
normal.cn: chest 本是箱子，而肋骨至今仍在心脏周围围成一只箱子。

normal.en: A chest of drawers is a box grown legs and handles.
normal.cn: chest of drawers 就是长出腿和把手的箱子。

normal.en: Get it off your chest: say the worry out loud and feel lighter.
normal.cn: get it off your chest：把心事说出来，就会轻松一些。

normal.en: Chest pain, chest cold, chest X-ray: medical phrases keep the body sense.
normal.cn: chest pain、chest cold、chest X-ray，这些医学搭配保留身体义。

normal.en: The plural chests adds an s to both the box and the body.
normal.cn: 复数 chests 对箱子和胸部同样只加 s。

abstract.en: Picture a brass lock catching light on an old wooden lid.
abstract.cn: 想象旧木箱盖上铜锁反着光。

abstract.en: Picture a hand pressed flat against a heartbeat.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手平放在跳动的心口。

abstract.en: Picture a drawer sliding open on folded shirts.
abstract.cn: 想象抽屉滑开，露出叠好的衬衫。

examples.en: The nurse listened to his chest and took notes.
examples.cn: 护士听了他的胸部，做了记录。

examples.en: An old chest stood at the foot of the bed.
examples.cn: 床脚放着一只旧箱子。

examples.en: She keeps her winter clothes in the chest of drawers.
examples.cn: 她把冬衣放在五斗柜里。

dict_mnemonic.text: chest 像一只箱子：木箱装东西，胸腔装心肺，抽屉柜装衣服。

root: 源自希腊语 kiste（箱子），经拉丁语 cista 与古英语 cest 进入英语，十六世纪起兼指胸腔。

sensesIntro.en: The stored box is the oldest sense, the body borrowed its shape, and the furniture borrowed its name.
sensesIntro.cn: 储物箱是最古老义项，身体借用了它的形状，家具又借用了它的名称。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a lidded container that holds something precious inside.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只带盖、内装贵重之物的容器。

branches.en: The body sense names the rib cage.
branches.cn: 身体义项指肋骨围成的胸腔。

branches.en: The box sense keeps the lid and the lock.
branches.cn: 箱子义项保留盖与锁。

branches.en: The furniture sense adds drawers to the box.
branches.cn: 家具义项给箱子添上抽屉。

branches.en: Both senses share the container image.
branches.cn: 两个义项共享容器意象。

branches.en: A chest of drawers is a box made for a bedroom.
branches.cn: 五斗柜是为卧室改造的箱子。

intro.en: Chest stays one short stem through its plural and its two derivatives.
intro.cn: chest 在复数与两个派生词中保持同一个短词干。

latinIntro.en: Latin cista, a box, comes from Greek kiste and gives English chest.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 cista（箱子）来自希腊语 kiste，并给出英语的 chest。

items.meaning: the body front or a strong box

items.example: Two chests stood in the hall.
The child had a chesty cough.

items.meaning: as much as a chest holds
items.example: A chestful of old maps was found.
items.exampleCN: 发现了满满一箱旧地图。

items.example: The drawer stuck in damp weather.
items.exampleCN: 潮湿天气里抽屉会卡住。

items.meaning: one of the curved bones of the chest

items.exampleCN: cista 变成古英语的 cest。

latinEntries.example: Cista is the direct source of chest.
latinEntries.exampleCN: cista 是 chest 的直接来源。

latinEntries.example: Kiste is the oldest layer of the word.
latinEntries.exampleCN: kiste 是这个词最古老的一层。
